Volume 262 Biographies 21: Li Gu, Zan Jurun, Dou Zhengu, Li Tao, Wang Yijian, Zhao Shangjiao, Zhang Xi, Zhang Zhu, Bian Guidang, Liu Wensou, Liu Tao, Bian Guangfan, Liu Zai, Cheng Yu

1
李穀，字惟珍，潁州汝陰人。 身長八尺，容貌魁偉。 少勇力善射，以任俠為事，頗為鄉人所困，發憤從學，所覽如宿習。 年二十七，舉進士，連辟華、泰二州從事。
Li Gu, whose style name was Weizhen, came from Ruyin in Ying Prefecture. He stood eight chi tall, with a grand and imposing bearing. As a youth he was strong and skilled at archery and lived by chivalrous deeds, which brought him much trouble from his neighbors. In anger he turned to study, and everything he read seemed already familiar to him. At twenty-seven he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to serve as adjutant in Hua and Tai prefectures.
2
開運二年秋，出為磁州刺史、北面水陸轉運使。 契丹入汴，少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。 穀曰：“臣無狀，負陛下。 ”因傾囊以獻。 會契丹主發使至州，穀禽斬之，密送款於漢祖，潛遣河朔酋豪梁暉入據安陽，契丹主患之，即議北旋。
In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyun he was appointed prefect of Ci Prefecture and commissioner for north-route water and land transport. When the Khitan entered Bian, the young emperor was carried north in disgrace. None of the former ministers dared to attend him, but Gu alone bowed to welcome him on the road, and ruler and minister wept as they faced each other. Gu said, "Your servant is unworthy and has failed Your Majesty." He then emptied his purse and offered it to him. When the Khitan ruler sent envoys to the prefecture, Gu seized and executed them, secretly pledged allegiance to the founder of Han, and covertly sent the Hebei chieftain Liang Hui to occupy Anyang. Troubled by this, the Khitan ruler at once considered withdrawing north.
3
會有告契丹以城中虛弱者，契丹還攻安陽，陷其城，穀自郡候契丹，遂見獲。 契丹主先設刑具，謂之曰：“爾何背我歸太原？ ”穀曰：“無之。 ”契丹主因引手車中，似取所獲文字，而穀知其詐，因請曰：“如實有此事，乞顯示之。 ”契丹國制，人未伏者不即置死。 自後凡詰穀者六次，穀詞不屈。 契丹主病，且曰：“我南行時，人云爾謂我必不得北還，爾何術知之？ 今我疾甚，如能救我，則致爾富貴。 ”穀曰：“實無術，蓋為人所陷耳。 ”穀氣色不撓，卒寬之。
Someone informed the Khitan that the city was weak. They returned to attack Anyang, took the city, and when Gu went from his prefecture to wait upon the Khitan, he was captured. The Khitan ruler first set out instruments of torture and said to him, "Why did you betray me and go over to Taiyuan?" Gu said, "There was no such thing." The Khitan ruler reached into the cart as if to take out captured documents, but Gu knew it was a ruse and said, "If this truly happened, I beg you to show me." Under Khitan law, a man who had not yet submitted was not immediately put to death. After that he was interrogated six times in all, and each time Gu's answers did not waver. When the Khitan ruler fell ill, he said, "When I marched south, people said you declared I would never return north. What art told you that?" Now my illness is grave. If you can cure me, I will make you rich and honored. Gu said, "I truly have no art for that. I was simply framed by others." Gu's bearing did not falter, and in the end he was spared.
4
俄而德光道殂，永康繼立，署穀給事中。 時契丹將麻答守真定，而李崧、和凝與家屬皆在城中。 會李筠、何福進率兵逐麻答，推護聖指揮使白再榮權知留後。 再榮利崧等家財，令甲士圍其居以求賂，既得之，復欲殺崧等滅口。 穀遽見再榮謂之曰：“今國亡主辱，公輩握勁兵，不能死節，雖逐一契丹將，城中戰死者數千人，非獨公之力也。 一朝殺宰相，即日中原有主，責公以專殺，其將何辭以對？ ”再榮甚懼，崧等獲免。
Before long Deguang died on the road. Yongkang succeeded him and appointed Gu Supervising Censor. At that time the Khitan general Maduo held Zhending, and Li Song, He Ning, and their families were all inside the city. When Li Yun and He Fujin led troops to drive Maduo out, they installed Bai Zairong, Guardian of the Sacred Commander, as acting military governor. Zairong coveted the wealth of Song and the others and sent armed men to surround their homes demanding bribes. Once he had the money, he wanted to kill Song and the others to silence them. Gu hurried to see Zairong and said, "The state is destroyed and the sovereign humiliated, yet you hold strong troops and could not die for your principles. Though you drove out one Khitan general, several thousand men died fighting in the city—not by your strength alone." Kill a chief minister in the morning, and that very day the Central Plains will have a ruler who will charge you with murder on your own authority. What answer will you give then? Zairong was greatly frightened, and Song and the others were spared.
5
漢初，入拜左散騎常侍。 舊制，罷外郡歸本官，至是進秩，獎之也。 俄權判開封府。 時京畿多盜，中牟尤甚，穀誘邑人發其巢穴。 有劉德輿者，梁時屢攝畿佐，居中牟，素有幹材，穀即署攝本邑主簿。 浹旬，穀請侍衛兵數千佐德輿，悉禽賊黨，其魁一即縣佐史，一御史臺吏。 搜其家，得金玉財貨甚眾，自是行者無患。 俄遷工部侍郎。
At the beginning of the Han dynasty he entered court and was appointed Left Regular Cavalryman Attendant-in-Ordinary. Under the old rule, leaving an outer prefecture meant returning to one's original office; now he was promoted in rank as a reward. Before long he was made acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture. Bandits were numerous in the capital region, especially around Zhongmou. Gu induced local men to expose their hideouts. There was a man named Liu Deyu who during the Liang had repeatedly served in the capital region and lived in Zhongmou, a man of proven ability. Gu immediately appointed him acting chief clerk of the county. Within ten days Gu requested several thousand palace guards to assist Deyu. They captured the entire band, whose leaders were a county assistant clerk and a censorate clerk. Searching their homes turned up great quantities of gold, jade, and goods. From then on travelers went unharmed. Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
6
周祖西征，為西南面行營水陸轉運使。 關右平，改陳州刺史。 會有內難，急召赴闕。 周祖兵入汴，命權判三司。 廣順初，加戶部侍郎。 未幾，拜中書侍郎、平章事，仍判三司。 初，漢乾祐中，周祖討河中，穀掌轉運，時周祖已有人望，屬漢政紊亂，潛貯異志，屢以諷穀，穀但對以人臣當盡節奉上而已。 故開國之初，倚以為相。 是歲，淮陽吏民數千詣闕請立生祠，許之，穀懇讓得止。
When the Zhou founder campaigned west, Gu served as commissioner for water and land transport of the southwestern campaign army. When the region west of the passes was pacified, he was made prefect of Chen. When internal troubles broke out, he was urgently summoned to court. When the Zhou founder's army entered Bian, he was ordered to serve as acting administrator of the Three Departments. At the beginning of Guangshun he was made Vice Minister of Revenue. Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, while continuing to administer the Three Departments. Earlier, during the Qianyou era of Han, when the Zhou founder attacked Hezhong, Gu managed transport. The Zhou founder already enjoyed great popular regard, and with Han government in chaos he secretly harbored other ambitions and often hinted at them to Gu. Gu would only reply that a minister ought to exhaust his loyalty in serving the throne. For this reason, at the founding of the dynasty he was relied upon as chief minister. That year several thousand officials and commoners from Huaiyang came to court asking that a living shrine be erected in his honor. Permission was granted, but Gu earnestly declined and the plan was dropped.
7
先是，禁牛革法甚峻，犯者抵死。 穀乃校每歲用革之數，凡田十頃歲出一革，餘聽民私用。 又奏罷屯田務，以民隸州縣課役，盡除宿弊。 穀父祖本居河南洛陽，經巢之亂，園廬蕩盡，穀生於外。 既貴，訪得舊地，建蘭若，又立垣屋，凡族人之不可仕者分田居之。 詔改清風鄉高陽里為賢相鄉勳德里。
Previously the law against cattle hide had been very strict, and violators were punished with death. Gu then calculated the annual quota of hide: one hide per year for every ten qing of farmland, with the remainder left for private use by the people. He also memorialized to abolish the military colony offices and assign the people to prefectural and county tax duties, thereby removing long-standing abuses. Gu's father and grandfather had originally lived in Luoyang in Henan. During the Huang Chao rebellion their gardens and houses were utterly destroyed, and Gu was born away from home. Once he had risen high in rank he found the old site, built a Buddhist temple, and erected walls and houses, allotting fields and dwellings to kinsmen who could not take office. An edict renamed Qingfeng Township's Gaoyang Lane to Worthy Minister Township, Lane of Meritorious Virtue.
8
二年，晨起仆階下，傷右臂，在告，旬中三上表辭相位，周祖不允，免朝參，視事本司，賜白藤肩輿，召至便殿勉諭。 穀不得已，起視事。 征兗州，為東京留守、判開封府事。
In the second year he fell on the steps one morning and injured his right arm. While on leave he submitted three memorials within ten days asking to resign the chief ministry. The Zhou founder refused, exempted him from court attendance, let him conduct business in his own office, granted him a white rattan sedan chair, and summoned him to the side hall to encourage him. Gu had no choice but to rise and resume his duties. When the campaign against Yanzhou was launched, he was made regent of the eastern capital and administrator of Kaifeng.
9
顯德初，加右僕射、集賢殿大學士。 從世宗征太原，遇賊於高平，匿山谷中，信宿而出，追及乘輿，世宗慰撫之。 世宗將趨太原，命穀先調兵食，又代符彥卿判太原行府事。 師還，進位司空、門下侍郎，監修國史。 穀以史氏所述本於起居注，喪亂以來遂廢其職，上言請令端明、樞密直學士編記言動，為內廷日曆，以付史官。 是歲，河大決齊、鄆，發十數州丁壯塞之，命穀領護，刻期就功。
At the beginning of Xiande he was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy. Accompanying Shizong on the campaign against Taiyuan, he encountered the enemy at Gaoping, hid in a mountain valley, and emerged after two nights. He caught up with the imperial carriage, and Shizong comforted him. As Shizong was about to press on to Taiyuan, he ordered Gu first to provision the troops and also to replace Fu Yanqing as administrator of the Taiyuan campaign headquarters. When the army returned, he was promoted to Grand Marshal and Vice Director of the Chancellery and was put in charge of compiling the national history. Gu observed that historical writing depends on the diary of attendance and conduct, a duty abandoned since the chaos of war. He memorialized asking that Hanlin academicians compile a record of words and deeds as an inner-court calendar to be handed to the historians. That year the Yellow River burst its banks in Qi and Yun. Corvée labor was levied from more than ten prefectures to block the breach, and Gu was ordered to supervise the work, with a fixed deadline for completion.
10
二年冬，議伐南唐，以穀為淮南道行營前軍都部署，兼知廬、壽等州行府事，忠武軍節度王彥副之，韓令坤以下十二將率從。 穀領兵自正陽渡淮，先鋒都將白延遇敗吳軍數千於來遠，又破千餘人於山口鎮，進攻上窯，又敗千餘眾，獲其小校數十人，長圍壽春。 南唐遣大將劉彥貞來援，穀召將佐謀曰：“今援軍已過來遠，距壽陽二百里，舟棹將及正陽。 我師無水戰之備，萬一斷橋梁，隔絕王師，則腹背受敵矣。 不如退守浮梁，以待戎輅之至。 ”初，世宗至圉鎮，已聞此謀，亟走內侍乘驛止之。 穀已退保正陽，仍焚芻糧，回軍之際，遞相掠奪，淮北役夫數百悉陷於壽春。 世宗聞之怒，亟命李重進率師伐之，以穀判壽州行府。 是秋，詔歸闕，得風痹疾，告滿百日，累表請致仕，優詔不允。 每軍國大事，令中使就第問之。
In the winter of the second year they deliberated attacking Southern Tang. Gu was made overall commander of the advance army of the Huainan campaign headquarters and concurrently put in charge of the campaign offices of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures. Wang Yan, military commissioner of Zhongwu, served as his deputy, and twelve generals including Han Lingkun followed him. Gu led his troops across the Huai from Zhengyang. His advance commander Bai Yanyu defeated several thousand Wu troops at Laiyuan, broke another thousand at Shankou, attacked Shangyao and defeated over a thousand more, captured several dozen junior Wu officers, and laid a long siege to Shouchun. Southern Tang sent the great general Liu Yanzhen to relieve the siege. Gu summoned his officers and said, "The relief army has already passed Laiyuan and is two hundred li from Shouyang. Their boats will soon reach Zhengyang." Our army is not prepared for naval combat. If they cut the bridges and cut off the imperial army, we will be attacked from front and rear. It would be better to withdraw and hold Fuliang until the imperial carriage arrives. Earlier, when Shizong reached Yuzhen, he had already heard of this plan and urgently sent a palace attendant by post relay to stop it. Gu had already withdrawn to Zhengyang and even burned fodder and grain. On the retreat the troops plundered one another, and several hundred laborers north of the Huai were all lost at Shouchun. Shizong was furious when he heard this and urgently ordered Li Chongjin to lead troops against the enemy, appointing Gu administrator of the Shouzhou campaign office. That autumn an edict recalled him to court. He contracted wind paralysis, took leave for a full hundred days, and repeatedly memorialized to retire, but gracious edicts refused his request. Whenever a major affair of state arose, palace envoys were sent to his residence to consult him.
11
四年春，吳人壁紫金山，築甬道以援壽春，不及者數里。 師老無功，時請罷兵為便，世宗令范質、王溥就穀謀之。 穀手疏請親征，有必勝之利者三，世宗大悅，用其策。 及淮南平，賞賜甚厚。 出穀疏，令翰林學士承旨陶穀為讚以賜之。 是夏，世宗還，穀扶疾見便殿，詔令不拜，命坐御坐側。 以抱疾既久，請辭相位。 世宗怡然勉之，謂曰：“譬如家有四子，一人有疾，棄而不養，非父之道也。 朕君臨萬方，卿處輔相之位，君臣之間，分義斯在，奈何以祿奉為言。 ”穀愧謝而退。 俄以平壽州，敘功加爵邑。 是秋，穀抗表乞骸骨，罷相，守司空，加邑封，令每月肩輿一詣便殿，訪以政事。
In the spring of the fourth year the Wu fortified Purple Gold Mountain and built a raised passage to relieve Shouchun, but it fell short by several li. The army grew weary without success, and many at the time urged withdrawing the troops as the expedient course. Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Gu. Gu personally memorialized asking the emperor to campaign in person, citing three advantages that guaranteed victory. Shizong was greatly pleased and adopted his plan. When Huainan was pacified, his rewards were very generous. Gu's memorial was published, and Hanlin Academician Receiver Tao Gu was ordered to compose a eulogy to bestow on him. That summer, when Shizong returned, Gu was received in the side hall despite his illness. An edict ordered him not to bow and commanded him to sit beside the imperial seat. Because his illness had long endured, he asked to resign the chief ministry. Shizong cheerfully encouraged him, saying, "It is like a household with four sons. If one falls ill and is cast aside without care, that is not how a father should act." I rule the myriad realms, and you occupy the post of chief minister. The bond between ruler and minister lies in duty, not in salary and rank alone. Gu withdrew in shame and gratitude. Soon, for pacifying Shouzhou, his merit was reckoned and his noble fief was increased. That autumn Gu firmly memorialized asking to retire. He was dismissed from the chief ministry but retained as Grand Marshal with an increased fief, and was ordered once a month to come by sedan chair to the side hall to be consulted on government affairs.
12
五年夏，世宗平淮南回，賜穀錢百萬、米麥五百斛、芻粟薪炭等。 恭帝即位，加開府儀同三司，進封趙國公。 求歸洛邑，賜錢三十萬，從其請。 太祖即位，遣使就賜器幣。 建隆元年，卒，年五十八。 太祖聞之震悼，贈侍中。
In the summer of the fifth year, when Shizong returned from pacifying Huainan, he bestowed on Gu a million cash, five hundred hu of grain, and fodder, fuel, and other supplies. When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Gu was made Provisionally Honored with the Three Dignities and advanced to Duke of Zhao. He asked to return to Luoyang. Three hundred thousand cash was granted him, and his request was granted. When Taizu took the throne, envoys were sent to his home to bestow vessels and silks. In the first year of Jianlong he died at the age of fifty-eight. When Taizu heard the news he was deeply shaken and grieved and posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant.
13
穀為人厚重剛毅，深沉有城府，雅善談論，議政事能近取譬，言多詣理，辭氣明暢，人主為之聳聽。 人有難必救，有恩必報。 好汲引寒士，多至顯位。 與韓熙載善，熙載將南渡，密告穀曰：“若江東相我，我當長驅以定中原。 ”穀笑曰：“若中原相我，下江南探囊中物耳。 ”穀後果如其言。 李昉嘗為穀記室，在淮上被病求先歸。 穀視之曰：“子他日官祿當如我。 ”昉後至宰相、司空。
Gu was a man of weight, firmness, and resolution, deep and calculating. He was elegantly skilled in discourse; when discussing government he could draw apt comparisons from nearby matters, his words mostly reached the heart of the matter, and his tone was clear and flowing, so that rulers listened with rapt attention. If anyone was in hardship he surely rescued them; if anyone showed him favor he surely repaid it. He loved to lift up poor scholars, many of whom rose to prominent rank. He was on good terms with Han Xizai. When Xizai was about to cross south, he secretly told Gu, "If the lands east of the river make me chancellor, I shall drive far north and pacify the Central Plains." Gu laughed and said, "If the Central Plains make me chancellor, taking Jiangnan will be like reaching into a bag for what is already inside." Later events proved Gu's words true. Li Fang had once served as Gu's registry clerk. While on the Huai he fell ill and asked to return home first. Gu looked at him and said, "One day your office and emolument will be like mine." Fang later rose to chief minister and Grand Marshal.
14
周顯德中，扈載以文章馳名，樞密使王樸薦令知制誥。 除書未下，樸詣中書言之。 穀曰：“斯人薄命，慮不克享耳。 ”樸曰：“公在衡石之地，當以材進人，何得言命而遺才。 ”載遂知制誥，遷翰林學士，未幾卒。 世謂樸能薦士，穀能知人。 穀歸洛中，昭義李筠以穀周朝名相，遺錢五十萬，他物稱是，穀受之。 既而筠叛，穀憂恚而終。 子吉至補闕，拱至太子中允。
During the Xiande era of Zhou, Hu Zai was famed for his literary talent, and Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu recommended him to draft edicts. Before the appointment edict was issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to speak of it. Gu said, "This man's fate is thin. I fear he will not live to enjoy the appointment." Pu said, "Sir, you stand where the scales weigh. You ought to advance people by talent. How can you speak of fate and abandon worth?" Zai then became drafter of edicts, was transferred to Hanlin Academician, and before long died. People said Wang Pu could recommend talent and Li Gu could discern character. When Gu returned to Luoyang, Li Yun of Zhaoyi, taking him for a famous chief minister of the Zhou court, sent five hundred thousand cash and comparable gifts in kind, and Gu accepted them. Before long Yun rebelled, and Gu died of grief and distress. His son Ji rose to Remonstrating Censor, and Gong to Attendant in the Crown Prince's palace.
15
昝居潤
Zan Jurun
16
昝居潤，博州高唐人。 善書計。 後唐長興中，隸樞密院為小吏，以謹願稱。 晉初，出掌滑州廩庾，遂補牙職。 會景延廣留守西洛，署為右職。 延廣卒，居潤往依陝帥白文珂，文珂致仕，乃表薦居潤於周祖。
Zan Jurun came from Gaotang in Bo Prefecture. He was skilled in writing and accounting. During the Changxing era of Later Tang he served the Bureau of Military Affairs as a junior clerk and was known for diligence and sincerity. At the beginning of Jin he was sent to manage the granaries of Hua Prefecture and was then appointed to a staff post in the military headquarters. When Jing Yanguang served as regent of the western capital, he appointed Zan to a senior staff post. When Yanguang died, Jurun went to serve under Bai Wenke, the military governor of Shaanxi; after Wenke retired, he memorialized the throne recommending Jurun to Zhou Taizu.
17
太祖立，加檢校太尉。 及征澤、潞，命赴澶州巡警。 師還，權知鎮州，加左領軍衛上將軍。 建隆二年，又權知澶州。 八月，拜義武軍節度，在鎮數年，得風痹，詔還京師。 乾德四年，卒，年五十九，贈太師。
When Emperor Taizu ascended the throne, Jurun was given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor. During the campaign against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to Duan Prefecture to conduct patrol and inspection duties. After the army returned, he served as acting prefect of Zhenzhou and was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Imperial Guard. In the second year of the Jianlong era, he again served as acting prefect of Duanzhou. In the eighth month he was made military governor of the Yiwu Army. After several years in the province he developed paralysis from wind affliction, and an imperial edict recalled him to the capital. In the fourth year of Qiande he died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
18
居潤性明敏，有節概，篤於行義。 初，晉室將亡，景延廣委其族自洛赴難，至則為遼人所執。 遼人在洛者遽欲恣摽掠，延廣僚吏部曲悉遁，獨居潤力保護，其家以安。 居潤與太祖同事世宗，情好款浹，嘗薦沈倫於太祖，以為純謹可用，後至宰相，世稱其知人。
Jurun was quick-witted and perceptive, possessed firmness of character, and was deeply committed to doing what was right. Earlier, as the Jin dynasty was nearing its end, Jing Yanguang sent his kinsmen from Luoyang to join him in his emergency, but they were captured by the Khitans upon arrival. The Khitans in Luoyang at once tried to plunder without restraint. Yanguang's staff and retainers all fled, but Jurun alone worked to protect the family, and they remained secure. Jurun had served Emperor Shizong alongside Taizu, and the two were on terms of warm friendship. He once recommended Shen Lun to Taizu as honest, careful, and fit for office; Shen later rose to grand chancellor, and people praised Jurun for discerning talent.

子惟質至內園使，弟居濟至水部員外郎。 大中祥符三年，錄其孫建中為三班借職。
His son Weizhi rose to Commissioner of the Inner Park, and his younger brother Juji to Outer Gentleman in the Ministry of Waterworks. In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, his grandson Jianzhong was granted an honorary post as borrowed officer of the Third Rank.

竇貞固
Dou Zhengu

天福三年，詔百僚各上封事，貞固疏曰：“臣聞舉善為明，知人則哲。 聖君在位，藪澤豈有隱淪； 昭代用材，政理固無紊亂。 求賢若渴，從諫如流，鄭所以譽子皮； 囗囗囗囗，囗囗囗囗，魯所以譏文仲。 為國之要，進賢是先。 陛下方樹丕基，宜求多士。 乞降詔百僚，令各司議定一人，有何能識，堪何職官，朝廷依奏用之。 若能符薦引，果謂當才，所奏之官，望加獎賞； 如乖其舉，或涉徇私，所奏之官，宜加黜罰。 自然官由德序，位以才升。 三人同行，尚聞擇善； 十目所視，必不濫知。 臣職在論思，敢陳狂狷。 ”書奏，帝深嘉之，命所司著為令典。 明年，改御史中丞，與太常卿崔棁、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允同詳定正冬朝會禮節、樂章及二舞行列。 歷刑部、門下二侍郎。
In the third year of Tianfu, the court ordered every official to submit a sealed memorial. Zhengu wrote: "I have heard that to elevate the worthy is enlightenment, and to know men is wisdom. When a sage ruler sits upon the throne, how could talent remain hidden in marsh and fen; In an enlightened age that puts talent to use, government and order will surely never fall into confusion. Thirsting for the worthy as for water, heeding remonstrance as a flowing stream—therefore Zheng criticized Zi Pi; [text missing in source], [text missing in source], therefore Lu criticized Wen Zhong. The first duty of governing a state is to advance the worthy. Your Majesty is now laying a lasting foundation; you should seek out men of talent in great number. I beg that Your Majesty issue an edict to the hundred officials, directing each department to select one man after deliberation, stating what talents he possesses and what office he can fill, so that the court may appoint him as recommended. If the recommendation proves accurate and the man is truly the right talent, the official who submitted the memorial should be rewarded; If the recommendation misses the mark or involves private favoritism, the official who submitted it should be demoted and punished. Then offices will naturally be ordered by virtue, and rank will rise according to talent. When three men walk together, one can still learn to choose the good among them; With ten eyes upon a man, judgment will surely not be applied carelessly. My duty is to deliberate and advise; I dare offer this blunt and presumptuous counsel. " When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor greatly praised it and ordered the responsible office to codify it as a standing regulation. The following year he was made Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, together with Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Shuai, Vice Minister of Punishments Lu Qi, and Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, worked out in detail the rites of the winter court assembly, the musical sections, and the formations of the two ritual dances. He served in turn as Vice Minister of Punishments and Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

少帝即位，拜工部尚書。 遷禮部尚書，知貢舉。 舊制，進士夜試，繼以三燭。 長興二年改令晝試，貞固以晝晷短，難盡士材，奏復夜試。 擇士平允，時論稱之。 改刑部尚書，出為潁州團練使。 歲餘，復拜刑部尚書。
When the Young Emperor came to the throne, Zhengu was appointed Minister of Works. He was transferred to Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the civil service examinations. Under the old system, jinshi candidates were examined at night, with three candles allowed for the session. In the second year of Changxing the rule was changed to daytime examinations. Zhengu argued that the daylight hours were too short to fully test scholarly talent and memorialized to restore night examinations. In selecting candidates he was fair and even-handed, and public opinion praised him. He was made Minister of Punishments and sent out as military training commissioner of Ying Prefecture. After a little more than a year, he was again appointed Minister of Punishments.

漢祖入汴，貞固與禮部尚書王松率百官見於滎陽西，漢祖駐駕，勞問久之。 初營宗廟，帝以姓自漢出，遂襲國號，尊光武為始祖，並親廟為五。 詔群臣議，貞固上言曰：“按《王制》：‘天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。 ’《正義》曰：‘周之制七廟者，太祖及文王、武王之祧與親廟四也。 ’又曰：‘七廟者，據周也。 有其人則七，無其人則五。 ’至光武中興，及魏、晉、宋、齊、隋、唐，或立六廟，或立四廟，蓋建國之始，未盈其數也。 《禮》曰‘德厚者流光’，此天子可以祀六世之義也。 今陛下大定寰區，重興漢祚，旁求典禮，用正宗祧，伏請立高、曾、祖、禰四親廟。 及自古聖王祖有功、宗有德、更立始祖在四廟之外，不拘定數，所以或五廟或七廟。 今請尊高皇帝、光武皇帝為始祖，法文王、武王不遷之制，用歷代六廟之規，庶合典禮。 ”漢祖從之。 論者以天子建國，各從其所起，堯自唐侯，禹生大夏是也。 立廟皆祖其有功，商之契，周之後稷，魏之武帝，晉之三廟是也。 高祖起於晉陽，而追嗣兩漢，徒以同姓為遠祖，甚非其義； 貞固又以四親匹庶，上合高、光，失之彌遠矣。 但援立親廟可也，餘皆非禮。 俄遷吏部尚書。
When Han Taizu entered Bian, Zhengu and Minister of Rites Wang Song led the hundred officials to meet him west of Xingyang. Han Taizu halted his carriage and questioned and comforted them at length. When the ancestral temple was first established, the emperor, holding that his surname sprang from Han, accordingly adopted that dynastic name, honored Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestor, and together with the ancestral temples made five in all. An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate. Zhengu submitted a memorial saying: "According to the Royal Regulations: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples; feudal lords have five; grand masters three; officers one. ' The Correct Meaning says: 'The Zhou system of seven temples comprises the founding ancestor, the distant temples of King Wen and King Wu, and four ancestral temples.' ' It also says: 'Seven temples refers to the Zhou model.' 'When there are such men, there are seven; when there are not such men, there are five.' ' From Guangwu's restoration down through Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Sui, and Tang, some dynasties established six temples and some four, because at the founding of a state the full number had not yet been reached. The Rites says, 'Those of deep virtue shed light afar'—this is the principle by which the Son of Heaven may sacrifice to six generations. Now Your Majesty has greatly settled the realm, revived the Han destiny, and broadly sought ritual precedents to establish the legitimate ancestral line. I respectfully request establishing four ancestral temples for great-grandfather, grandfather, father, and immediate forebear. Moreover, from antiquity sage emperors and ancestral kings who had merit to the clan or virtue to honor have additionally established a founding ancestor outside the four temples, not bound to a fixed number—hence sometimes five temples and sometimes seven. Now I request honoring Emperor Gao and Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestors, following the system by which King Wen and King Wu are not moved, and employing the six-temple precedent of successive dynasties, so that the arrangement may accord with ritual canon. " Han Taizu accepted the proposal. Commentators held that when the Son of Heaven founds a state, each follows the place from which he rose: Yao from Lord of Tang, Yu born in Great Xia—such were the cases. In establishing temples, all venerate those who had merit to the clan: Qi of Shang, Hou Ji of Zhou, Emperor Wu of Wei, the three temples of Jin—such were the cases. The High Emperor rose at Jinyang, yet traced succession to the two Han dynasties, making distant forebears merely by shared surname—this was greatly contrary to principle; Zhengu further treated the four ancestral temples as equal to those of commoners while placing them above Gao and Guangwu—the error was all the greater; Only supporting the establishment of the four ancestral temples was acceptable; the rest were all contrary to ritual. Soon afterward he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

周祖兵起，貞固與蘇逢吉奉隱帝兵次於野，敗。 逢吉倉黃自殺，貞固遂詣周祖。 周祖稱太后制，委貞固與蘇禹珪、王峻同掌軍國政事。 周祖登位，加兼侍中。 會以馮道為首相，改監修國史。 俄罷相，守司徒，封沂國公。 世宗即位，以范質為司徒，貞固遂歸洛陽，輸課役，齒為編民。 貞固不能堪，訴於留守向拱，拱不聽。
When Zhou Taizu raised his army, Zhengu and Su Fengji accompanied Emperor Yin with troops encamped in the field and were defeated. Fengji, in sudden panic, killed himself, and Zhengu then went to Zhou Taizu. Zhou Taizu issued an order in the Empress Dowager's name, entrusting Zhengu with Su Yugui and Wang Jun jointly to manage military and state affairs. When Zhou Taizu ascended the throne, Zhengu was additionally appointed Concurrent Palace Attendant. When Feng Dao was appointed chief chancellor, Zhengu was reassigned as supervising compiler of dynastic history. Soon removed from the chancellorship, he retained the post of Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yi. When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Fan Zhi was made Minister of Works. Zhengu then returned to Luoyang, paid taxes and corvée labor, and was registered on the rolls as an ordinary subject. Zhengu could not endure this and appealed to the regent Xiang Gong, but Gong would not listen.

宋初，以前三公赴闕陪位，詣范質，求任東宮三少，預朝請，質不為奏。 乃還洛，放曠山水，與布衣輩攜妓載酒以自適。 開寶二年病困，自為墓誌，卒，年七十八。
At the beginning of the Song dynasty, former Three Dukes went to court to attend investiture ceremonies. Zhengu called on Fan Zhi and requested appointment as one of the Three Minor Tutors of the Eastern Palace with permission to attend court, but Zhi would not submit a memorial on his behalf. He then returned to Luoyang, roamed freely among mountains and rivers, and with commoners took courtesans and wine for his own pleasure. In the second year of Kaibao, gravely ill, he composed his own epitaph and died at the age of seventy-eight.

李濤，字信臣，京兆萬年人。 唐敬宗子郇王瑋十世孫。 祖鎮，臨濮令。 父元，將作監。 朱梁革命，元以宗室懼禍，挈濤避地湖南，依馬殷，署濤衡陽令。 濤從父兄郁仕梁為閣門使，上言濤父子旅湖湘，詔殷遣歸京師，補河陽令。
Li Tao, styled Xinchen, came from Wannian in Jingzhao. He was a tenth-generation descendant of Prince Ye of Yun, son of Emperor Jingzong of Tang. His grandfather Zhen served as magistrate of Linpu. His father Yuan served as Director of Palace Construction. When the Zhu Liang dynasty replaced Tang, Yuan, fearing calamity as a member of the imperial clan, took Tao and fled to Hunan, relying on Ma Yin, who appointed Tao magistrate of Hengyang. Tao's father's elder brother's son Yu served Liang as Gate Commander and submitted a memorial that Tao and his father were sojourning in Hunan and Xiang. An edict ordered Yin to send them back to the capital, and Tao was appointed magistrate of Heyang.

At the beginning of Tiansheng in Later Tang, he passed the jinshi examination in the first class. From staff member in Jin Prefecture he was appointed Investigating Censor, then promoted to Right Remonstrating Censor. When Prince of Song Wang Conghou governed Yecheng, he appointed Tao administrative adjutant for Weibo observation. After a little more than a year, he entered court as Drafting Attendant of the Household.

晉天福初，改考功員外郎、史館修撰。 晉祖幸大梁，張從賞以盟津叛，陷洛陽，扼虎牢。 故齊王全義子張繼祚者實黨之，晉祖將族其家。 濤上疏曰：“全義歷事累朝，頗著功效。 當巢、蔡之亂，京師為墟，全義手披荊棘，再造都邑，垂五十年，洛民賴之。 乞以全義之故，止罪繼祚妻子。 ”從之。 嘗奉詔為宋州括田使，前雄州刺史袁正辭齎束帛遺濤，以田園為託，濤表其事，晉祖嘉之。 正辭坐降一階，濤遷浚儀令。 改比部郎中、鹽判官，改刑部郎中。
At the beginning of Tianfu in Jin, he was transferred to Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, Outer Section, and historiographer in the History Institute. When Jin Taizu visited Daliang, Zhang Congshang rebelled at Mengjin, captured Luoyang, and seized Hulao Pass. The former Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi's son Zhang Jizu was in fact his partisan, and Jin Taizu was about to exterminate his entire family. Tao submitted a memorial saying: "Quanyi served successive courts and achieved considerable merit. During the disorders of Huang Chao and Cai, the capital lay in ruins. Quanyi personally cleared through thorns and brambles and rebuilt the city. For nearly fifty years the people of Luoyang relied upon him. I beg that for Quanyi's sake punishment be limited to Jizu's wife and children alone. " The emperor agreed. He once received an edict to serve as land survey commissioner for Song Prefecture. The former prefect of Xiong Prefecture, Yuan Zhengcí, brought silks as a gift to Tao and entrusted his fields and gardens to him. Tao memorialized the matter, and Jin Taizu praised him. Zhengcí was demoted one rank for the offense, and Tao was promoted to magistrate of Junyi. He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and salt commissioner, then to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

涇帥張彥澤殺記室張式，奪其妻，式家人詣闕上訴。 晉祖以彥澤有軍功，釋其罪。 濤伏閣抗疏，請置於法。 晉祖召見諭之，濤植笏叩階，聲色俱厲，晉祖怒叱之，濤執笏如初。 晉祖曰：“吾與彥澤有誓約，恕其死。 ”濤厲聲曰：“彥澤私誓，陛下不忍食其言； 范延光嘗賜鐵券，今復安在？ ”晉祖不能答，即拂衣起，濤隨之，諫不已。 晉祖不得已，召式父鐸、弟守貞、子希範等皆拜以官，罷彥澤節製。 濤歸洛下，賦詩自悼，有“三諫不從歸去來”之句。 先是，范延光據鄴叛，晉祖賜鐵券許以不死，終亦不免，故濤引之。 晉祖崩，濤坐不赴臨，停。 未幾，起為洛陽令，遷屯田職方郎中、中書舍人。
The military governor of Jing, Zhang Yanze, killed his recorder Zhang Shi and seized his wife. Shi's family went to the palace gate to lodge a complaint. Jin Taizu, because Yanze had military merit, released him from punishment. Tao submitted a memorial from within the gate in protest, requesting that Yanze be punished according to law. Jin Taizu summoned him for an audience and tried to persuade him. Tao planted his tablet and knocked it on the steps, his voice and bearing both fierce. Jin Taizu angrily shouted at him, but Tao held his tablet as before. Jin Taizu said, "I have a sworn pact with Yanze and have promised to spare his life. " Tao said sharply, "Yanze's oath was a private pledge. Your Majesty is unwilling to break your word; Fan Yanguang was once granted an iron certificate promising he would not be executed—where is it now? " Jin Taizu had no reply. He brushed his robes and stood up at once. Tao followed him, remonstrating without letup. Jin Taizu had no choice. He summoned Shi's father Duo, his younger brother Shouzhen, his son Xifan, and the rest, appointing them all to office, and stripped Yanze of his military commission. Tao returned to Luoyang and wrote a poem of self-lament containing the line, "Three remonstrances rejected—I return whence I came." Earlier, when Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion, Jin Taizu had granted him an iron certificate promising he would not be executed, yet in the end he was not spared—therefore Tao invoked this precedent. When Jin Taizu died, Tao was punished for failing to attend the mourning rites and was suspended from office. Before long he was recalled as magistrate of Luoyang, then promoted to Gentleman of the Bureau of Tuntian and Fang and Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

會契丹入汴，彥澤領突騎入京城，恣行殺害，人皆為濤危之。 濤詣其帳，通刺謁見。 彥澤曰：“舍人懼乎？ ”濤曰：“今日之懼，亦猶足下昔年之懼也。 向使先皇聽僕言，寧有今日之事。 ”彥澤大笑，命酒對酌，濤神氣自若。
When the Khitans entered Bian, Yanze led crack cavalry into the capital and slaughtered without restraint. Everyone feared for Tao's life. Tao went to his tent and sent in a visiting card to request an audience. Yanze said, "Are you afraid, Deputy Director? " Tao said, "The fear I feel today is no different from the fear you once felt yourself. If the late emperor had listened to me, would any of this have happened? " Yanze laughed loudly, ordered wine, and they drank together. Tao remained perfectly composed.

漢祖起義至洛，濤自汴奉百官表入對，漢祖問京師財賦，從契丹去後所存幾何，濤具對稱旨，漢祖嘉之。 至汴，以為翰林學士。 杜重威據鄴叛，高祖命高行周、慕容彥超討之，二帥不協。 濤密疏請親征。 高祖覽奏，以濤堪任宰輔，即拜中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事。
When Han Taizu raised his revolt and reached Luoyang, Tao brought the memorial of all officials from Bian for an audience. Han Taizu asked how much revenue the capital still held after the Khitans withdrew. Tao answered in full to the emperor's satisfaction, and Han Taizu praised him. When they reached Bian, he was appointed Hanlin Academician. Du Chongwei held Ye in rebellion. Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him, but the two commanders failed to cooperate. Tao sent a secret memorial asking the emperor to lead the campaign in person. Gaozu read the memorial and judged Tao fit for chief minister. He was at once appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Minister of Revenue and Participant in Determining Affairs of State.

隱帝即位，楊邠、周祖共掌機密，史弘肇握兵柄，與武德使李鄴等中外爭權，互作威福。 濤疏請出邠等藩鎮，以清朝政。 隱帝不能決，白於太后，太后召邠等諭之，反為所構，免相歸第。 時中書廚釜鳴者數四，濤晝寢閣中，夢嚴飾廳事，群吏趨走，云迎新宰相帶諸司使，既寤，心異之。 數日濤罷，以邠為相兼樞密使。 及周祖舉兵，太后倉皇涕泣曰：“不用李濤之言，宜其亡也。 ”
When Yin Emperor ascended the throne, Yang Bin and Zhou Taizu jointly handled confidential affairs. Shi Hongzhao held military power, and he, Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye, and others fought for authority inside and outside the court, each wielding power for personal gain. Tao memorialized asking that Bin and the others be posted to military governorships so that court governance might be cleared up. Yin Emperor could not decide and reported the matter to the empress dowager. She summoned Bin and the others to admonish them, but they slandered her in return. Tao was dismissed as chancellor and sent home. At the time the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen rang several times. Tao napped in his pavilion by day and dreamed of a grandly decorated hall where clerks hurried about, saying a new chancellor was arriving who would also hold the various commissioner posts. When he awoke, he found it strange. Several days later Tao was dismissed, and Bin was made chancellor while also serving as Commissioner of Military Affairs. When Zhou Taizu raised his army, the empress dowager wept in alarm and said, "We did not heed Li Tao's advice. No wonder the dynasty is falling. "

周初，起為太子賓客，歷刑部、戶部二尚書。 世宗宴駕，為山陵副使。 恭帝即位，封莒國公。
At the beginning of the Zhou dynasty, he was recalled as Guest of the Heir Apparent and then served successively as Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue. When Emperor Shizong died, he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb. When Gongdi ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.

宋初，拜兵部尚書。 建隆二年，濤被病。 有軍校尹勳董浚五丈河，陳留丁壯夜潰，勳擅斬隊長陳琲等十人，丁夫七十人皆杖一百，刵其左耳。 濤聞之，力疾草奏，請斬勳以謝百姓。 家人謂濤曰：“公久病，宜自愛養，朝廷事且置之。 ”濤憤言曰：“人孰無死，但我為兵部尚書，坐視軍校無辜殺人，烏得不奏？ ”太祖覽奏嘉之，詔削奪勳官爵，配隸許州。 濤卒，年六十四，贈右僕射。
At the beginning of the Song dynasty, he was appointed Minister of War. In the second year of Jianlong, Tao fell ill. A camp officer named Yin Xun was supervising dredging of the Wuzhang River when the conscript laborers of Chenliu broke away one night. Xun on his own authority executed squad leader Chen Bei and nine others—ten men in all—and had all seventy laborers beaten one hundred strokes and their left ears cut off. When Tao heard of this, though gravely ill he drafted a memorial asking that Xun be executed to appease the people. His family said to Tao, "You have been ill for a long time. You should look after yourself and leave court affairs aside for now. " Tao said angrily, "Who does not die? But I am Minister of War. If I sit by while a camp officer kills innocent people, how can I fail to memorialize? " Taizu read the memorial and praised it. An edict stripped Xun of rank and title and assigned him as convict labor in Xuzhou. Tao died at sixty-four and was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
35
濤慷慨有大志，以經綸為己任。 工為詩，筆劄遒媚，性滑稽，善諧謔，亦未嘗忤物，居家以孝友聞。 景德三年，其孫惟勤詣闕自陳，詔授許州司士參軍。 子承休至尚書水部郎中，承休子仲容。
Tao was bold and ambitious, taking the governance of the realm as his personal duty. He was skilled at poetry and wrote with force and grace. By nature he was witty and fond of banter, yet never gave offense. At home he was known for filial piety and brotherly devotion. In the third year of Jingde, his grandson Weiqin appeared at court to petition in person and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xuzhou by edict. His son Chenxiu rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Waterworks in the Secretariat. Chenxiu's son was Zhongrong.
36
弟澣
Younger brother: Huan
37
濤弟澣，字日新。 幼聰敏，慕王、楊、盧、駱為文章。 後唐長興初，吳越王錢騑卒，詔兵部侍郎楊凝式撰神道碑，令澣代草，凡萬餘言，文彩遒麗，時輩稱之。 秦王從榮召至幕中，從榮敗，勒歸田里。 久之，起為校書郎、集賢校理。 晉天福中，拜右拾遺，俄召為翰林學士。 會廢學士院，出為吏部員外郎，遷禮部郎中、知制誥。 復置翰林，遷中書舍人，再為學士。 時濤在西掖，縉紳榮之。
Tao's younger brother Huan, style name Rixin. From youth he was bright and quick, and he took Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo as models in literary composition. At the start of the Changxing era in Later Tang, the King of Wuyue died. An edict ordered Vice Minister of War Yang Ningshi to compose the spirit-way stele, but Huan was told to draft it in his stead. The text ran to more than ten thousand characters, its prose forceful and beautiful, and contemporaries praised it. The Prince of Qin, Congrong, summoned him to his staff. When Congrong was defeated, Huan was forced to return to his home district. After some time he was recalled as Proofreader and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies. During the Tianfu era of Jin he was appointed Remonstrance Officer on the Right, and soon after was summoned as Hanlin Academician. When the Hanlin Academy was abolished, he was sent out as Outer Deputy Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites with responsibility for drafting edicts. When the Hanlin Academy was restored, he was promoted to Deputy Director of the Secretariat and again became an academician. At the time Tao served in the Western Secretariat wing, and court officials regarded the brothers with admiration.
38
契丹入汴，澣與同職徐台符俱陷塞北。 永康王兀欲襲位，置澣宣政殿學士。 兀欲死，述律立，以其妻族蕭海貞為幽州節度使。 海貞與澣相善，澣乘間諷海貞以南歸之計，海貞納之。
When the Khitans entered Bian, Huan and his colleague Xu Taifu both fell captive north of the frontier. Prince Yongkang Wuyu seized the throne and appointed Huan Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall. When Wuyu died, Shulü was enthroned and appointed Xiao Haizhen, a member of his wife's clan, military governor of Youzhou. Haizhen was on friendly terms with Huan. Huan seized an opportunity to suggest to Haizhen a plan to return south, and Haizhen accepted it.
39
周廣順二年，澣因定州孫方諫密表言契丹衰微之勢，周祖嘉焉，遣諜者田重霸齎詔慰撫，仍命澣通信。 澣復表述契丹主幼弱多寵，好擊鞠，大臣離貳，若出師討伐，因與通好，乃其時也，請速行之。 屬中原多事，不能用其言。
In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou, Huan sent a secret memorial through Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou describing the Khitans' decline. Zhou Taizu was pleased and dispatched the agent Tian Chongba with an edict of consolation, while also ordering Huan to maintain correspondence. Huan again reported that the Khitan ruler was young and weak, surrounded by favorites, and fond of cuju, while his great ministers were divided. If an army were sent on campaign and friendly ties established at the same time, this would be the moment, he urged, and asked that it be done at once. Just then the Central Plains were beset by many troubles, and his advice could not be adopted.
40
澣在契丹嘗逃歸，為其所獲，防禦彌謹。 契丹應曆十二年六月卒，時建隆三年也。 濤收澣文章編之為《丁年集》。 澣二子，承確，主客郎中，承續，職方郎中。
While among the Khitans Huan once tried to escape and return south, but was captured and guarded more strictly thereafter. He died in the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yingli under the Khitans, which corresponded to the third year of Jianlong. Tao collected Huan's writings and compiled them into the Dingnian Collection. Huan had two sons: Chenque, Gentleman of the Bureau of Hosts and Guests, and Chenxu, Gentleman of the Bureau of Fang.
41
孫仲容
Grandson: Zhongrong
42
仲容，字儀父，舉進士甲科，除大理評事、知三原縣。 累擢監察御史，為殿試進士考官。 真宗問題義，對稱旨，詔試中書，擢左司諫、直史館。 天聖中，以起居郎為知制誥，累遷右諫議大夫。 在西掖八年，次當補學士，而不為宰相張士遜所喜，罷為給事中、集賢院學士、判史館、司農寺，復知制誥。 及石中立、張觀補學士，始以為翰林侍讀學士。 久之，兼龍圖閣學士，至戶部侍郎卒。
Zhongrong, style name Yifu, passed the jinshi examination in the top tier and was appointed Reviewing Official of the Grand Court of Justice and magistrate of Sanyuan County. He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor and served as examiner for the palace jinshi examination. Emperor Zhenzong questioned him on the meaning of the Classics, and his answers pleased the emperor. An edict tested him at the Secretariat and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Officer and Compiler at the Historical Archives. During the Tiansheng era he served as drafter of edicts while holding the post of Gentleman for Attending Affairs, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance and Policy Adviser. After eight years in the Western Secretariat wing, it was his turn to be appointed Hanlin Academician, but Grand Chancellor Zhang Shixun did not favor him. He was dismissed to serve as Attendant Imperial Counselor, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Commissioner for the Historical Archives and Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, while again holding responsibility for drafting edicts. When Shi Zhongli and Zhang Guan were appointed academicians, he was at last made Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician. After some time he concurrently served as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and died while holding the post of Vice Minister of Revenue.
43
仲容性醇易，喜飲酒，不與物忤，與人言，未嘗及勢利。 三弟早卒，字其諸孤十餘人如己子，當世稱其長者。 然於吏事非所長。 自集制草為《冠鳳集》十二卷。
Zhongrong was mild and easygoing. He loved wine, gave no offense, and in conversation with others never spoke of power or profit. Three younger brothers died early. He educated more than ten orphaned nephews as if they were his own sons, and his age called him a man of virtue. Yet he was not strong in administrative affairs. He himself compiled his draft edicts into the Guanfeng Collection in twelve juan.
44
王易簡
Wang Yijian
45
王易簡，字國寶，京兆萬年人。 性介特寡合。 曾祖朏，唐劍州刺史。 祖遠，連州刺史。 父貫，唐州刺史。 易簡少好學，工詩。 會僖宗幸蜀，長安兵亂，避地山谷。 梁乾化中，邵王友誨鎮陝，易簡舉進士，詣府拔解，友誨贈錢二十萬。 明年遂擢第，復隱華山。 邠帥韓恭辟觀察支使。 府罷，華帥李保衡復辟從事。 逾年，尹皓代保衡，易簡仍在幕府。
Wang Yijian, style name Guobao, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao. He was upright and aloof by nature and did not easily agree with others. His great-grandfather Fei served as prefect of Jian Prefecture under Tang. His grandfather Yuan served as prefect of Lian Prefecture. His father Guan served as prefect of Tang Prefecture. From youth Yijian loved learning and was skilled at poetry. When Emperor Xizong went to Shu, troops rioted in Chang'an, and Yijian fled to the mountain valleys. During the Ganhu era of Liang, Prince of Shao Youhui governed Shaan. Yijian entered the jinshi examination, went to the prefectural office for release from the local quota, and Youhui gave him two hundred thousand cash. The next year he passed the examination and again retired to Mount Hua. The military governor of Bin, Han Gong, recruited him as Administrative Assistant of the Observation Commission. When that prefectural office closed, the governor of Hua, Li Baoheng, recruited him again as a staff officer. More than a year later Yin Hao replaced Baoheng, and Yijian remained on the staff.
46
會朱友謙以河中叛歸莊宗，攻華州甚急，城中危懼，咸請築月城以自固。 皓恃勇不聽，下令曰：“有敢復言者斬。 ”易簡固請，乃許。 板築始畢，外城果壞，軍民賴之。 會夜不能攻，友謙遂遁去。 皓卒，易簡歸田里。 久之，召為著作郎，數月棄去。 復召為右拾遺，上書忤旨，出為鄧州節度推官。
When Zhu Youqian rebelled with Hezhong and submitted to Zhuangzong, pressing the attack on Hua Prefecture, the city was gripped by fear. Everyone urged building an outer semicircular wall for self-defense. Hao relied on his courage and would not listen. He ordered, "Whoever dares speak of this again shall be executed. " Yijian urgently petitioned again, and only then was permission granted. As soon as the plank-wall construction was finished, the outer wall indeed collapsed, and soldiers and civilians owed their safety to it. When night fell the attackers could not press the assault, and Youqian withdrew. When Hao died, Yijian returned to his home district. After some time he was summoned as Archivist, but within months he resigned. He was again summoned as Remonstrance Officer on the Right, but a memorial displeased the throne and he was sent out as judicial investigator under the military governor of Dengzhou.
47
晉初，賜金紫，判弘文館、史館事。 晉祖為治務求速效，易簡上《漸治論》以諫之，詔書褒答，以論付史館。 及廢翰林學士，易簡兼知內制，又拜御史中丞，歷右丞、吏部侍郎、左丞、判吏部銓。 嘗上言：“選門格敕條件具存，藩府官僚習熟者少，凡給文解，未曉規程，以致選人詣都，親求解樣，往來跋涉，重可傷閔，傳寫少差，旋復驗放。 乞自今委南曹詳定解樣，兼錄長定格取解條，下諸州，板置州院門，每取解時，準條式遵行。 ”從之。 晉祖在大梁，臺省湫隘，易簡奏舉故事，一歲得元省錢二百萬，繕治省署及造器物，號為舉職。
At the beginning of Jin he was granted gold and purple rank insignia and served as commissioner for the Hall of Spread Culture and the Historical Archives. Jin Taizu in governing sought quick results. Yijian submitted the "Gradual Governance Discourse" to remonstrate with him. An edict praised and answered him, and the essay was deposited in the Historical Archives. When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Yijian concurrently handled inner court drafting. He was also appointed Censor-in-Chief and then served successively as Right Vice Censor, Vice Minister of Personnel, Left Vice Censor, and Commissioner for Personnel Selection in the Ministry of Personnel. He once submitted: "The regulations and edict provisions governing the selection gate are all on record, yet few officials in the military prefectures are familiar with them. Whenever credentials are issued, they fail to understand the rules, so candidates must come to the capital in person to request specimen forms—traveling back and forth at great hardship, a matter deeply pitiable—and slight errors in transcription lead at once to rejection and release. He requested that from now on the Southern Office be charged with carefully determining the specimen credential form, that the provisions for obtaining credentials from the Changding regulations also be recorded and distributed to all prefectures, posted on boards at prefecture gate offices, and that whenever credentials were submitted for the examination, the rules and formats be followed accordingly. The request was approved. When Jin Taizu was at Daliang, the central offices were cramped. Yijian memorialized proposing ancient precedents and in one year obtained two million strings of cash from the original provincial budget, repaired the provincial offices, and manufactured utensils—a performance termed "fulfilling one's duties."
48
周朝諱“簡”，易止名易。 廣順初，遷禮部尚書。 是冬，合三銓為一，令易簡權判，俄改刑部尚書。 周祖將親郊，命判兵部，會冊四廟，命為副使。 周祖晏駕，為山陵副使。 顯德四年，告老，以太子少保致仕，歸鄉里。
The Zhou court tabooed the character "Jian," so Yi dropped the character from his name and was known simply as Yi. At the start of Guangshun he was transferred to Minister of Rites. That winter the three selection bureaus were combined into one, and Yi was ordered to serve as acting commissioner. Soon afterward he was transferred to Minister of Punishments. When Zhou Taizu was about to perform the suburban sacrifice in person, Yi was ordered to serve as commissioner of the Ministry of War. When the four ancestral temples were enfeoffed, he was appointed deputy envoy. When Zhou Taizu died, Yi served as deputy envoy for the imperial tomb. In the fourth year of Xiande he requested retirement on grounds of age, retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and returned to his home district.
49
宋初，召加少傅。 所居華陰，構一鳴堂、二品樓，優遊自適。 建隆四年四月，無疾卒，年七十九。 子景讓，進士及第，至尚書郎。
At the beginning of Song he was summoned and promoted to Junior Grand Tutor. At his residence in Huayin he built the Hall of One Cry and the Second-Rank Tower, living at ease in comfort. In the fourth month of the fourth year of Jianlong he died without illness at age seventy-nine. His son Jingrang passed the jinshi examination and rose to Secretary in the Imperial Secretariat.
50
趙上交
Zhao Shangjiao
51
趙上交，涿州范陽人。 本名遠，字上交，避漢祖諱，遂以字稱。 祖光鄴，鄂州錄事參軍。 父簡章，涿州司馬。 上交身長七尺，黑色，美風儀，善談論，負才任氣，為鄉里所推。
Zhao Shangjiao came from Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture. His original name was Yuan and his style name was Shangjiao. To avoid the taboo of Han Taizu, he was thereafter known by his style name. His grandfather Guangye served as administrative aide of E Prefecture. His father Jianzhang served as vice prefect of Zhuo Prefecture. Shangjiao stood seven chi tall, with a dark complexion, handsome bearing, and skill in discourse. Proud of his talent and self-assured, he was esteemed by his community.
52
後唐同光中，嘗詣中山干王都。 有和少微者亦在都門下，忌之，頗毀訾上交，都遂不為禮。 上交不得志，因南遊洛陽，與中官驃騎大將軍馬紹宏善。 紹宏領北面轉運制置大使，表為判官，遷殿中丞。 秦王從榮開府兼判軍衛，以上交為虞部員外郎，充六軍諸衛推官。 李澣、張沆、魚崇遠皆白衣在秦府，悉與上交友善。 累遷司封郎中，充判官。 從榮素豪邁，不遵禮法，好昵群小。 上交從容言曰：“王位尊崇，當修令德以慰民望，王忍為此，獨不見恭世子、戾太子之事乎？ ”從榮怒出之，歷涇、秦二鎮州節度判官。 從榮及禍，僚屬皆坐斥，上交由是知名。
During the Tongguang era of Later Tang he once went to Zhongshan to seek audience with Wang Du. One He Shaowei was also in Du's retainer circle. Jealous of Shangjiao, he slandered him at length, and Du then showed him no courtesy. Unable to achieve his aims, Shangjiao traveled south to Luoyang and became friendly with the eunuch Commander-in-Chief of the Right, Ma Shaohong. Shaohong held the post of commissioner for north-route transport and supply. He recommended Shangjiao as adjutant, and Shangjiao was promoted to Palace Aide. When the Prince of Qin, Congrong, opened a princely establishment and concurrently served as commissioner of the military guard, Shangjiao was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and served as judicial reviewer for the Six Armies and various guard units. Li Huan, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan were all commoners in the Qin princely establishment, and Shangjiao befriended them all. He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites and served as adjutant. Congrong was naturally bold and unrestrained, failed to observe rites and law, and was fond of associating with petty men. Shangjiao spoke calmly and said, "The princely position is exalted. You ought to cultivate virtue to satisfy the people's hopes. How can you bear to do this? Have you not seen what befell Crown Prince Shen and Crown Prince Li?" Congrong was angered and dismissed him. Shangjiao then served successively as adjutant to the military governors of Jing and Qin prefectures. When Congrong met disaster, all his staff were dismissed and punished. Shangjiao thereby became well known.
53
晉初，召為左司郎中、度支判官，歷右諫議大夫。 會廢翰林學士，以上交為中書舍人、知內外制，遷刑部侍郎。 嘗上言：“伏睹長興中詔書：‘州縣官在任詳讞刑獄、昭雪人命者，不限歲月赴選，許令超資注官，仍賜章服。 諸道州府給付公驗，躬赴行部投狀，隨給優牒，庶絕欺罔，以存激勸。 ’載詳元詔，止言州縣，未該內外職司。 乞自今但能雪活冤獄，不限中外官，並加旌賞。 諸道州縣委長吏抄案以聞。 俟本人考滿，即詣刑部投狀，毋得隔越年歲，庶使內外同律。 ”詔從之。 俄遷戶部侍郎，拜御史中丞，彈舉無所阿避。
At the beginning of Jin he was summoned as Director in the Left Secretariat and fiscal adjutant, then served as Right Remonstrating Censor. When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Shangjiao was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat and charged with inner and outer court drafting, then promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments. He once submitted, "I respectfully observe the edict of the Changxing era: 'For prefectural and county officials who during their tenure carefully review criminal cases and exonerate the wrongly condemned, regardless of how many months before selection they may come, they are permitted to be registered for office above their normal grade and are granted ceremonial robes.'" Each circuit and prefecture shall issue official travel documents; the official shall personally go to the circuit headquarters to submit a petition, and a certificate of merit shall be issued promptly, so that deceit may be eliminated and incentive preserved. Upon examining the original edict, it speaks only of prefectural and county officials and does not cover inner and outer court offices. He requested that from now on whoever could exonerate the wrongly condemned and save lives, regardless of whether they were inner or outer court officials, should all receive commendation and reward. Each circuit and prefecture should entrust the chief official to copy the case record and report it. When the official himself completed his term of evaluation, he should go to the Ministry of Punishments to submit his petition and must not skip years in between, so that inner and outer offices might be judged by the same rule. An edict approved the request. Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief. In impeachments he showed favor to none.
54
契丹入汴，立明宗幼子許王從益為帝，以禮部尚書王崧為左丞相，上交為右丞相。 契丹去，上交請去偽號，稱梁王。 漢祖將至，從益遣上交馳表獻款，授檢校禮部尚書、太僕卿，遷秘書監。 周祖監國，命太師馮道迎湘陰公於徐州，以上交副之。
When the Khitan entered Bian, they installed Mingzong's young son, Prince Xu Congyi, as emperor, appointing Minister of Rites Wang Song as Left Chancellor and Shangjiao as Right Chancellor. After the Khitan departed, Shangjiao requested removal of the false imperial title and that Congyi be called Prince of Liang. When Han Taizu was about to arrive, Congyi sent Shangjiao with a fast dispatch to submit allegiance. Shangjiao was appointed Honorary Minister of Rites and Grand Master of the Stable, then transferred to Director of the Imperial Library. When Zhou Taizu served as regent, he ordered Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome the Duke of Xiangyin from Xuzhou, with Shangjiao as deputy.
55
廣順初，拜禮部侍郎。 會將試貢士，上交申明條制，頗為精密，始復糊名考校。 擢扈載甲科，及取梁周翰、董淳之流，時稱得士。 轉戶部侍郎。 明年再知舉，謗議紛然。 時樞密使王峻用事，常薦童子，上交拒之。 峻怒，奏上交選士失實，貶商州司馬，朝議以為太重，會峻貶乃止，但坐所取士李觀、侯璨賦落韻，改太子詹事。
At the start of Guangshun he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites. When the examination of tribute scholars was about to be held, Shangjiao clarified the regulations with considerable precision and for the first time restored sealed-name examination. He selected Hu Zai for first rank and also admitted Liang Zhouhan, Dong Chun, and others. At the time this was called having obtained worthy men. He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue. The following year he again served as chief examiner, and criticism arose on all sides. At the time Director of Military Affairs Wang Jun wielded power and often recommended youths, but Shangjiao refused them. Jun was angered and memorialized that Shangjiao's selection of scholars was false. Shangjiao was demoted to Vice Prefect of Shang Prefecture, but court opinion held this excessive, and when Jun himself was demoted the sentence was halted. Because the scholars he had selected, Li Guan and Hou Can, had failed rhyme in their fu compositions, however, he was punished and made Crown Prince's Household Administrator.
56
顯德初，遷賓客。 二年，拜吏部侍郎，多請告不朝，時出遊別墅。 世宗因問陶穀曰：“上交豈衰老乎？ ”穀對曰：“上交昔掌貢舉，放鬻市家子李觀及第，受所獻名園，多植花卉，優遊自適。 ”世宗怒，免其官。
At the start of Xiande he was transferred to Guest of the Crown Prince. In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel. He frequently requested leave and did not attend court, often going out to his country villa. Shizong therefore asked Tao Gu, "Has Shangjiao perhaps grown old?" Tao Gu answered, "When Shangjiao formerly managed the tribute examination, he let a market merchant's son, Li Guan, pass and accepted from him a famed garden as a gift. He planted many flowers and lived at ease in comfort." Shizong was angered and removed him from office.
57
宋初，起為尚書右丞。 建隆二年正月，卒，年六十七。 上交所蒞官以幹聞，當時稱有公輔器。 尤好吟詠，有集二十卷，張昭為序。
At the beginning of Song he was recalled as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. In the first month of the second year of Jianlong he died at age sixty-seven. Shangjiao was known for competence when he took office, and at the time he was said to possess the makings of a chief minister. He was especially fond of composing poetry. He had a collection in twenty scrolls, for which Zhang Zhao wrote the preface.
58
子曮，字可畏。 七歲喪母過哀。 十二能屬文，與兄晙同舉進士，未成名而兄夭，遂以蔭補千牛備身，歷秘書郎、殿中丞、著作郎。 卒，年二十六。 有集十卷，太宗嘗取以入內。
His son Yan, whose style name was Kewei. At seven he mourned his mother with excessive grief. At twelve he could compose prose. He and his elder brother Jun both entered for the jinshi examination together, but before he had achieved fame his brother died young. He then entered office by inherited privilege as Personal Guard of the Thousand Oxen and served successively as Secretary, Palace Aide, and Archivist. He died at age twenty-six. He had a collection in ten scrolls, and Taizong once took it into the inner palace.
59
張錫，福州閩縣人。 梁末，劉君鐸任棣州刺史，辟為軍事判官。 棣為鄆之屬郡，郡有麴務，鄆以牙將主之，頗橫恣，民有犯麴三斤，牙將欲置於死，君鐸力不能救。 既而牙將盜麥百斛私造麴，事覺，錫判曰：“麴犯三斤，求生不克，麥盜百斛，免死誠難。 ”時郡吏以使府牙將乞免，錫不允，固置於法。
Zhang Xi came from Min County in Fu Prefecture. At the end of Liang, Liu Junduo served as prefect of Di Prefecture and summoned him as military adjutant. Di was a subordinate commandery of Yan. The commandery had a brewing monopoly, and Yan sent a military officer to oversee it who was quite overbearing. When a commoner violated the brewing law with three jin of mash, the military officer sought to put him to death, and Junduo lacked the power to save him. Later the military officer stole a hundred hu of wheat to brew mash privately. When the affair was discovered, Xi rendered judgment: "For a brewing offense of three jin, the man could not obtain life; for stealing a hundred hu of wheat, exemption from death is truly difficult." At the time commandery clerks, on behalf of the military governor's military officer, begged exemption, but Xi did not consent and firmly applied the law.
60
同光末，趙在禮舉兵於鄴，瀕河諸州多構亂，錫權知州事，即出省錢賞軍，皆大悅，一郡獨全，棣人賴之。 後為淄川令，不畏強禦，專務愛民，刺史有所徵，不答，由是銜之。 及代，白其事於宰相馮道。 道知錫介直，即奏召為監察御史，出為陝、虢觀察判官。 晉開運二年，拜右補闕，歷起居郎、刑部員外郎、開封府判官、浚儀令、司門駕部二郎中，並以清節聞。 周顯德中，以老疾求解官，授右諫議大夫致政。
At the end of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, and prefectures along the Yellow River largely fell into turmoil. Xi temporarily managed prefectural affairs and immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the troops. All were greatly pleased, and the commandery alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him. Later he served as magistrate of Zichuan. He feared no powerful oppressors and devoted himself to loving the people. When the prefect sought levies he did not respond, and for this the prefect bore a grudge. When his term ended, he reported the matter to Chancellor Feng Dao. Dao knew Xi's firm integrity and at once memorialized to summon him as Supervising Censor. Xi then went out as adjutant to the military governor of Shan and Guo circuits. In the second year of Kaiyun of Jin he was appointed Right Supplementation Censor and served successively as Diarist, Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments, adjutant of the Kaifeng prefectural government, magistrate of Junyi, and Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Ministry of War—all renowned for integrity. During Xiande of Zhou, on grounds of old age and illness he requested resignation and was granted retirement as Right Remonstrating Censor.
61
宋初，改給事中。 錫無子，宰相范質嘗兄事之，館於別墅。 錫以執政之門，不欲久處，往依鄉人鄧州觀察判官黃保緒。 建隆二年六月，卒於穰下。
At the beginning of Song he was reappointed Supervising Secretary. Xi had no son. Chancellor Fan Zhi once treated him as an elder brother and lodged him at his country villa. Being at the house of the chief minister, Xi did not wish to stay long and went to lodge with his fellow townsman Huang Baoxu, adjutant to the military governor of Deng Prefecture. In the sixth month of the second year of Jianlong he died at Rangxia.
62
張鑄，字司化，河南洛陽人。 性清介，不事生產。 曾祖居卿，祖裼，父文蔚，在唐俱舉進士。 裼至翰林學士承旨、天平軍節度、檢校吏部尚書。 文蔚，中書侍郎、平章事，《五代史》有傳。
Zhang Zhu, whose style name was Sihua, came from Luoyang in Henan. By nature upright and scrupulous, he did not engage in productive enterprise. His great-grandfather Jujing, grandfather Ti, and father Wenwei all passed the jinshi examination under Tang. Ti rose to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, military governor of Tianping, and Honorary Minister of Personnel. Wenwei served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor and has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

鑄，梁貞明三年舉進士，補福昌衛、集賢校理，拜監察御史，遷殿侍御史。 仕後唐，歷起居郎、金部員外郎，賜緋，改右司員外郎。
Zhu passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhenming of Liang, was appointed to Fu Chang Guard and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was made Supervising Censor, and was promoted to Palace Censor. Serving Later Tang, he served successively as Diarist and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was granted purple rank insignia, and was transferred to Vice Director in the Right Secretariat.
64
明宗初，轉金部郎中，賜金紫。 嘗上言曰：“國家以務農為本，守令以勸課為先，廣辟田疇，用實倉廩。 竊見所在鄉村浮戶，方事墾辟，甫成生計，種田未至二頃，植木未及十年，縣司以定色役，民畏責斂，捨之而去，殊乖撫恤之方，徒設招攜之令。 望令諸州應有荒田縱民墾蒔，俟及五頃已上，三年外始聽差科。 ”從之。 使兩浙還，遷考功郎中。
At the beginning of Mingzong he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and granted gold and purple rank insignia. He once submitted, "The state takes devoted attention to agriculture as its foundation; local officials take exhortation of cultivation as their priority, broadly opening fields to fill the granaries. I have observed that in the villages, floating households who are in the midst of opening wasteland and have just established livelihoods—having cultivated less than two qing of fields and planted trees for less than ten years—when the county office fixes their tax and corvée assignments, the people fear levies and abandon the land and leave. This greatly contradicts the method of nurturing and soothing and empties the orders to attract and gather settlers." He hoped an order would be issued that in all prefectures wasteland should be left to the people to reclaim and sow, and that only after it reached five qing or more might corvée and tax be imposed after three years. The request was approved. After returning from a mission to the Two Zhes, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
65
鑄美姿儀，善筆劄，老能燈下細書如蠅頭。 由晉以來，天地、宗廟及上徽號、封拜王公冊文，皆詔鑄書之。 及卒，身無兼衣，家人鬻其服馬、園圃，得錢十萬以葬。
Zhu had a handsome appearance and was skilled at calligraphy. In old age he could write fine characters by lamplight like fly heads. From the Jin period onward, edicts for Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and imperial honorific titles, as well as investiture documents enfeoffing princes and dukes, were all ordered written by Zhu. When he died he had no spare garment. His family sold his riding robes and garden to obtain a hundred thousand cash for burial.

邊歸讜
Bian Guidang
67
邊歸讜，字安正，幽州薊人，父退思，檀州刺史。 歸讜弱冠以儒學名。 後唐末，客遊幷、邠。 晉祖鎮太原，召置門下，表為河東節度推官、試秘書省校書郎，改太原府推官、試大理評事。
Bian Guidang, whose style name was Anzheng, came from Ji in You Prefecture. His father Tuisi was prefect of Tan Prefecture. Guidang was famed for classical learning from young adulthood. At the end of Later Tang he traveled as a guest to Bing and Bin. When the founding emperor of Later Jin was stationed at Taiyuan, he summoned Guidang into his personal staff and memorialized for his appointment as investigating officer on the Hedong military commission and acting proofreader in the Secretariat. He was later reassigned as investigating officer of Taiyuan prefecture and acting judicial reviewer in the Grand Court.
68
天福初，拜監察御史。 歷殿中侍御史、禮部員外郎，充戶部判官。 遷水部郎中，賜金紫，拜比部郎中、知制誥。 歷右諫議大夫、給事中。 嘗上言：“使臣經過州縣，券料外妄自徵需，以豐傔從，多索人驢，用遞行李。 挾命為勢，淩下作威，供億稍遲，即加鞭箠，吏民受辱，寧免怨嗟。 欲望察訪得情，嚴示懲戒。 ”從之。 俄遷右散騎常侍。
At the beginning of the Tianfu era, he was appointed Supervising Censor. He served successively as Palace Attending Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and also held the post of chief clerk in the Ministry of Revenue. He was promoted to Director of the Water Bureau, granted gold and purple insignia, and appointed Director of the Tribute Bureau with responsibility for drafting imperial edicts. He served successively as Right Remonstrator and Chief of the Secretariat. He once submitted a memorial saying, "When envoys pass through prefectures and counties, they go beyond their authorized warrants and rations and levy demands at will to enlarge their retinues. They requisition people's donkeys in large numbers and use them to relay their baggage." They wield imperial orders as a source of power, bully their subordinates, and throw their weight around. If provisions are even slightly delayed, they immediately resort to whipping and beating. Officials and commoners suffer humiliation, and resentment is inevitable. I ask that the court investigate these matters thoroughly and impose strict punishment as a warning. The emperor approved the proposal. Soon afterward he was promoted to Right Regular Attendant.
69
漢初，歷禮部、刑部二侍郎。 時史弘肇怙權專殺，閭里告訐成風。 歸讜言曰：“邇來有匿名書及言風聞事，構害善良，有傷風化，遂使貪吏得以報復私怨，讒夫得以肆其虛誕。 請明行條制，禁遏誣罔。 凡顯有披論，具陳姓名。 其匿名書及風聞事者並望止絕。 ”論者韙之。
At the beginning of Later Han, he served successively as Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Punishments. At that time Shi Hongzhao wielded power and executed people at will, and mutual denunciation in neighborhoods had become widespread. Guidang said, "Recently anonymous letters and accusations based on hearsay have been used to frame and harm good people, damaging public morals. This allows corrupt officials to settle private scores and gives slanderers free rein to spread falsehoods. I ask that clear regulations be enforced to forbid and suppress false accusations. Whenever an accusation is made openly, the accuser's name should be fully disclosed. Anonymous letters and cases based on hearsay should both be abolished entirely. Commentators praised the proposal.
70
周廣順初，遷兵部、戶部二侍郎。 世宗聞其亮直，擢為尚書右丞、樞密直學士，以備顧問。 就轉左丞，世宗以累朝以來憲綱不振，命為御史中丞。
At the beginning of the Guangshun era under Later Zhou, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Revenue. Emperor Shizong, having heard of his candor and integrity, promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, so that he might be available for consultation. He was immediately transferred to Left Vice Director. Because censorial discipline had languished through successive reigns, Shizong appointed him Censor-in-Chief.

歸讜雖號廉直，而性剛介，言多忤物。 顯德三年冬，大宴廣德殿，歸讜酒酣，揚袂言曰：“至於一杯而已。 ”世宗命黃門扶出之。 歸讜回顧曰：“陛下何不決殺趙守微。 ”守微者，本村民，因獻策擢拾遺，有妻復娶，又言涉指斥，坐決杖配流，故歸讜語及之。 翌日，伏閣請罪，詔釋之，仍於閣門復飲數爵，以愧其心。 五年秋，歸讜與百官班廣德殿門外，忽厲聲聞於帝，詔奪一季奉。
Although Guidang was known for integrity and uprightness, he was by nature stern and uncompromising, and his words often gave offense. In the winter of the third year of Xiande, during a grand banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue, Guidang, already well into his cups, waved his sleeve and cried out, "It all comes down to a single cup!" Shizong ordered the palace eunuchs to escort him out. Guidang looked back and said, "Your Majesty, why not simply have Zhao Shouwei beaten to death?" Shouwei had originally been a village commoner. Because he submitted a policy proposal, he was promoted to Reminder. Though he already had a wife, he took another, and his words were also said to involve denunciation of the ruler. He was sentenced to beating with the execution stick and exile, which is why Guidang mentioned him. The next day he prostrated himself at the palace gate to beg forgiveness. An edict pardoned him, and at the Gate of the Secretariat he was given several more cups of wine, intended to make him feel ashamed. In the autumn of the fifth year, as Guidang stood in ranks with the other officials outside the gate of the Hall of Broad Virtue, a sharp voice suddenly reached the emperor. An edict stripped him of one season's salary.

宋初，遷刑部尚書。 建隆三年，告老，拜戶部尚書致仕。 乾德二年，卒，年五十七。 子定，雍熙二年進士及第。
At the beginning of the Song dynasty, he was promoted to Minister of Punishments. In the third year of Jianlong, he requested retirement on grounds of age and was appointed Minister of Revenue with permission to retire. He died in the second year of Qiande at the age of fifty-seven. His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi.
73
劉溫叟
Liu Wensou
74
劉溫叟，字永齡，河南洛陽人。 性重厚方正，動遵禮法。 唐武德功臣政會之後。 叔祖崇望，相昭宗。 父岳，後唐太常卿。 溫叟七歲能屬文，善楷隸。 岳時退居洛中，語家人曰：“吾兒風骨秀異，所未知者壽耳。 今世難未息，得與老夫皆為溫、洛之叟足矣。 ”故名之溫叟。 以蔭補國子四門助教，河南府文學。 清泰中，為左拾遺、內供奉。 以母老乞歸就養，改監察御史，分司。 時臺署廢弛，溫叟作新之。 未幾，召為右補闕。
Liu Wensou, whose style name was Yongling, came from Luoyang in Henan. He was grave, solid, and upright by nature, and in all his conduct he observed ritual and law. He was a descendant of Zhenghui, a meritorious minister of the Wude era under Tang. His granduncle Chongwang had served as chancellor under Emperor Zhaozong. His father Yue was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Later Tang. Wensou could compose prose at the age of seven and was skilled in regular and clerical script. Yue was then living in retirement in Luoyang and told his family, "My son's bearing is outstanding and unusual. The only thing we cannot yet know is how long he will live." The troubles of the age have not yet ceased. It would be enough if he and I could both grow old together as elders of Wen and Luo. That is why he was given the name Wensou, "Warm Elder." By yin privilege he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates at the Directorate of Education and Literary Officer of Henan prefecture. During the Qingtai era, he served as Left Reminder and Inner Attendant. Because his mother was elderly, he asked to return home to care for her and was reassigned as Supervising Censor with a detached post. At that time the censorate offices had fallen into neglect, and Wensou restored them. Before long he was summoned to serve as Right Supplementation Officer.
75
契丹入汴，溫叟懼，隨契丹北遷，與承旨張允共上表求解職。 契丹主怒，欲出允等為縣令。 趙延壽曰：“若學士才不稱職求解者，守本官可也，不可加貶出。 ”遂得罷職出院。 漢祖南下，溫叟自洛從至鄭州，稱疾不行。 及入汴，溫叟久之方至，授駕部郎中。
When the Khitan entered Bian, Wensou, in fear, followed them north in relocation. Together with Academician Recipient Zhang Yun, he submitted a memorial requesting release from office. The Khitan ruler was enraged and wished to demote Yun and the others to county magistrates. Zhao Yanshou said, "If academicians whose talents do not suit their posts request release, they may retain their original rank. They should not be further demoted and sent out." They were thus dismissed from office and allowed to leave the academy. When the founder of Later Han marched south, Wensou followed from Luoyang as far as Zhengzhou, then pleaded illness and went no farther. When the court entered Bian, Wensou arrived only after a long delay and was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau.
76
周初，拜左諫議大夫，逾年，改中書舍人，加史館修撰，判館事。 顯德初，遷禮部侍郎、知貢舉，得進士十六人。 有譖於帝者，帝怒，黜十二人，左遷太子詹事。 溫叟實無私，後數年，其被黜者相繼登第。 溫叟與張昭同修漢隱帝及周祖實錄，恭帝即位，遷工部侍郎兼判國子祭酒事。
At the beginning of Later Zhou, he was appointed Left Remonstrator. After a year he was reassigned as Drafting Secretary, with the added title of Compiler in the Historiography Institute and responsibility for its affairs. At the beginning of the Xiande era, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the examinations, selecting sixteen jinshi graduates. Someone slandered him to the emperor. The emperor was enraged, dismissed twelve of the graduates, and demoted Wensou to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent. Wensou had in fact shown no favoritism. Several years later, those who had been dismissed passed the examinations one after another. Wensou and Zhang Zhao jointly compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Yindi of Han and the Zhou founder. When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Wensou was promoted to Vice Minister of Works with concurrent charge of the Directorate of Education.
77
宋初，改刑部。 建隆九年，拜御史中丞。 丁內艱，退居西洛，旋復本官。 三年，兼判吏部銓。 因上言曰：“伏見兩京百司，漸乏舊人，多隳故事。 雖檢閱具存於往冊，而舉行須在於攸司。 蓋因年限得官，歸司者例與減選； 冬集赴調，授任者尋又出京。 兼有裁滿初官，不還舊局，但稱前資，用圖免役。 又有嘗因停任，切欲歸司，而元敕不該，無由復職。 遂使在司者失於教習，歷事者難於追還。 伏望自今諸司職掌，除官勒留及歸司者，如理減外欠三選以下，仍須在司執行公事，及三十月即許赴集； 如理選外欠三選以上，及在官不成資考者，即準元敕處分。 若在任停官及在司停職者，經恩後於刑部出給雪牒，卻勒歸司，如無闕員，即令守闕，餘依敕格處分。
At the beginning of the Song dynasty, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments. In the ninth year of Jianlong, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief. Upon entering mourning for his mother, he retired to western Luoyang, but soon resumed his original post. In the third year, he was given concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board. He submitted a memorial saying, "I observe that in the offices of the two capitals, veteran personnel are gradually disappearing and many established practices are being abandoned." Although the regulations still exist in the old registers, putting them into practice depends on the offices responsible for them. This is because officials who obtain posts through seniority, when they return to their bureaus, are by precedent given reduced selection priority; those who assemble in the winter for reassignment, once appointed, soon leave the capital again; there are also those who have barely completed their first term, do not return to their former bureau, but merely cite their previous rank in order to avoid service duties; and there are still others who, having once had their appointments suspended, earnestly wish to return to their bureaus, but because the original edict does not cover their case, they have no way to resume office. The result is that those who remain in the bureaus lack instruction and practice, while experienced officials are hard to bring back. I ask that from now on, for the duties of the various bureaus, except for officials forcibly retained and those returning to their bureaus: if beyond the proper reduction they owe fewer than three selection cycles, they should still perform official business in the bureau, and after thirty months be permitted to assemble for reassignment; if beyond the proper selection they owe three or more cycles, and those in office who fail to complete their qualification review, they should be handled according to the original edict; if suspended from office while in post or suspended from duty while in the bureau, after an amnesty the Ministry of Punishments should issue a certificate of rehabilitation and compel their return to the bureau; if there is no vacancy, let them hold a waiting post. All other cases should be handled according to edicts and regulations.
78
一日晚歸由闕前，太祖方與中黃門數人偶登明德門西闕，前騶者潛知之，以白溫叟。 溫叟令傳呼如常過闕。 翌日請對，具言：“人主非時登樓，則近制咸望恩宥，輦下諸軍亦希賞給。 臣所以嗬導而過者，欲示眾以陛下非時不登樓也。 ”太祖善之。 憲府舊例，月賞公用茶，中丞受錢一萬，公用不足則以贓罰物充。 溫叟惡其名不取。 任臺丞十二年，屢求代。 太祖難其人，不允。 開寶四年被疾，太祖知其貧，就賜器幣，數月卒，年六十三。
One day, as Wensou was returning late and passing before the gate-tower, Taizu happened to be ascending the western tower of the Gate of Bright Virtue with several inner palace eunuchs. The outriders secretly learned of this and informed Wensou. Wensou ordered the heralds to announce his passage as usual when crossing before the tower. The next day he requested an audience and explained in full, "When the ruler ascends a tower at an unscheduled time, those nearby all hope for grace and pardon, and the armies below the capital also expect rewards." The reason I had the heralds cry out and passed through as usual was to show everyone that Your Majesty does not ascend the tower at unscheduled times. Taizu approved of this. An old custom of the censorate provided monthly public-use tea. The Censor-in-Chief received ten thousand cash, and if public funds were insufficient, confiscated goods from corruption cases were used to make up the difference. Wensou disliked the taint associated with this practice and refused to accept the money. He served as head of the censorate for twelve years and repeatedly requested a successor. Taizu could find no suitable replacement and did not grant the request. In the fourth year of Kaibao he fell ill. Taizu, knowing he was poor, sent gifts of vessels and silks to his home. Several months later he died at the age of sixty-three.
79
溫叟事繼母以孝聞，雖盛暑非冠帶不敢見。 五代以來，言執禮者惟溫叟焉。 立朝有德望，精賞鑒，門生中尤器楊徽之、趙鄰幾，後皆為名士。 范杲幼時，嘗以文贄溫叟，大加稱獎，以女妻之。
Wensou was renowned for filial devotion to his stepmother. Even in the height of summer he would not visit her unless fully capped and girded. From the Five Dynasties onward, when people spoke of strict observance of ritual, they meant Wensou. In court he enjoyed moral stature and refined judgment. Among his students he especially valued Yang Huizhi and Zhao Linji, who later both became celebrated figures. When Fan Gao was young, he once presented a literary work to Wensou, who praised it highly and gave him his daughter in marriage.
80
太宗在晉邸，聞其清介，遣吏遺錢五百千，溫叟受之，貯廳西舍中，令府吏封署而去。 明年重午，又送角黍、執扇，所遣吏即送錢者，視西舍封識宛然，還以白太宗。 太宗曰：“我錢尚不用，況他人乎？ 昔日納之，是不欲拒我也； 今周歲不啟封，其苦節愈見。 ”命吏輦歸邸。 是秋，太宗侍宴後苑，因論當世名節士，具道溫叟前事，太祖再三賞歎。
When Taizong was at the Prince of Jin's residence, having heard of Wensou's integrity, he sent an official to present five hundred thousand cash. Wensou accepted the gift, stored it in the western wing of the hall, had the prefectural clerk seal it, and left. The next year at the Double Fifth festival he again sent rice dumplings and a hand fan. The official sent was the same one who had brought the money. Seeing that the seal on the western wing remained intact, he returned and reported this to Taizong. Taizong said, "Even my money he will not use—how much less anyone else's?" In accepting it then, he did not wish to reject me; now a full year has passed without the seal being broken. His austere integrity is all the more evident. He ordered the official to have the money carried back to the residence. That autumn, while attending a banquet in the rear garden, Taizong spoke of men of renown and integrity in the age and fully related Wensou's earlier conduct. Taizu repeatedly praised and sighed over it.
81
雍熙初，子炤罷徐州觀察推官待選，以貧詣登聞求注官。 及引對，太宗問誰氏子，炤以溫叟對。 太宗愀然，召宰相語其事，且言當今大臣罕有其比。 因問：“炤當得何官？ ”宰相言：“免選以為厚恩。 ”帝曰：“其父有清操，錄其子登朝，庶足示勸。 ”擢炤太子右讚善大夫，歷判三司理欠、憑由司，江南轉運司，入朝為司封郎中。 炳、燁並進士及第。
At the beginning of the Yongxi era, his son Zhao, having left the post of investigating officer under the Xuzhou observation commission and awaiting selection, went to the Petition Office to request an appointment because of poverty. When he was brought for audience, Taizong asked whose son he was. Zhao replied that he was Wensou's son. Taizong's expression turned grave. He summoned the chancellor to tell him the story and said that among the great ministers of the day, few could compare with Wensou. He then asked, "What office should Zhao receive?" The chancellor said, "Exemption from the selection process would be generous favor." The emperor said, "His father maintained pure integrity. Enrolling the son for court service would sufficiently serve as encouragement." Zhao was promoted to Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent. He served successively as chief judge of the Three Departments' Arrears and Credential Office and on the Jiangnan transport commission, and upon entering court became Director of the Office of Enfeoffment. Bing and Ye both passed the jinshi examination.
