子燁
Son: Ye
83
燁，字耀卿，進士及第。 積官秘書省著作郎。 知龍門縣，群盜殺人，燁捕得之，將械送府，恐道亡去，皆斬之。 眾服其果。 通判益州，召還，時王曙治蜀，或言其政苛暴。 真宗問：“曙治狀與淩策孰愈？ ”燁曰：“策在蜀，歲豐事簡，故得以寬假民。 比歲小歉，盜賊竊發，非誅殺不能禁。 然曙所行，亦未嘗出陛下法外。 ”帝善之。
Ye, whose style name was Yaoqing, passed the jinshi examination. He rose through successive appointments to Drafting Officer in the Secretariat. While serving as magistrate of Longmen County, Ye captured a band of murderers. He intended to send them to the prefectural seat in shackles, but fearing they might escape along the way, he had them all executed. The people admired his decisiveness. While serving as vice prefect of Yizhou, he was recalled to court. Wang Shu was then governing Shu, and some said his administration was harsh and severe. Emperor Zhenzong asked, "Whose record of governance is better—Wang Shu's or Ling Ce's?" Ye said, "When Ling Ce was in Shu, harvests were abundant and affairs were straightforward, so he could afford to be lenient toward the people." In recent years there have been minor crop failures, and banditry has begun to stir. Without executions it cannot be suppressed. Yet what Wang Shu has done has never exceeded the bounds of Your Majesty's laws. The emperor approved of this.
84
天禧元年，始置監官。 帝謂宰相曰：“諫官御史，當識朝廷大體。 ”於是以燁為右正言。 會歲薦饑，河決滑州，大興力役，饑殍相望。 燁請策免宰相，以應天變。 都城東南有泉出，民爭傳可以已疾，詔即其地建祥源觀。 燁言其詭妄不經，且亢旱，不可興土木以營不急； 又請罷提點刑獄，禁民棄父母事佛老者。 皆不報。
In the first year of Tianxi, supervisory censorial posts were established for the first time. The emperor told the chancellor, "Remonstrating officials and investigating censors ought to understand the court's larger principles." Thereupon Ye was appointed Right Rectifier. Famine struck year after year. The Yellow River broke its banks at Huazhou, massive corvée projects were launched, and starved corpses lined the roads. Ye requested that the chancellor be removed by imperial edict in response to this omen from heaven. A spring appeared southeast of the capital, and people spread the rumor that its water could cure illness. An edict ordered the construction of the Xiangyuan Temple on that spot. Ye argued that this was deceitful nonsense, and that amid severe drought one ought not undertake construction for nonessential purposes; He also called for abolishing judicial intendants and forbidding people to abandon their parents in order to follow Buddhism or Daoism. None of these memorials received a response.
85
表請補外，帝以燁屢言事，乃以判三司戶部勾院，出安撫京西。 還，直集賢院，同修起居注，遷右司諫。 以尚書工部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，權判吏部流內銓。 請京朝官遭父母憂，官司毋得奏留，故事當起復者如舊。 因詔益、梓、利、夔路長吏，仍舊奏裁，餘乞免持服者論其罪。 改三司戶部副使，擢龍圖閣待制，提舉諸司庫務，權發遣開封府事。 累遷刑部郎中、龍圖閣直學士、知河南府，徙河中府，卒。
He submitted a memorial requesting a provincial appointment. Because Ye had repeatedly remonstrated, the emperor made him chief auditor of the Three Departments Revenue Office and sent him out as Pacification Commissioner of Jingxi. Upon his return he served at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, jointly compiled the Veritable Records, and was promoted to censor in the Right Remonstrance Bureau. Serving as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat while also acting as Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, he held acting responsibility for the Ministry of Personnel's inward selection. He requested that when capital officials suffered parental bereavement, no office might memorialize to retain them, while established precedent allowing leave-from-mourning appointments would remain unchanged. Accordingly an edict ruled that the chief administrators of the Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui circuits might still submit such cases for imperial decision, while all others who sought exemption from mourning dress would be prosecuted. He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Three Departments Revenue Office, promoted to associate drafting officer of the Dragon Diagram Hall, placed in charge of the various warehouse offices, and given acting authority over Kaifeng prefectural affairs. He rose through successive promotions to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments and Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, served as prefect of Henan, was transferred to Hezhong, and died there.

初，王曙坐寇準貶官，在朝無敢往見者。 燁歎曰：“友朋之義，獨不行於今歟？ ”往餞之，經宿而還。 嘗善河中處士李瀆，瀆死，為陳其高行，詔以著作郎贈之。
Earlier, when Wang Shu was demoted on account of Kou Zhun, no one at court dared visit him. Ye sighed and said, "Has the bond of friendship alone ceased to be practiced in our age?" He went to send Wang Shu off and did not return until the following day. He had once been close to the recluse Li Du of Hezhong. When Du died, Ye set forth his lofty character, and an edict posthumously conferred on him the title of Drafting Officer.
87
唐末五代亂，衣冠舊族多離去鄉里，或爵命中絕而世系無所考。 惟劉氏自十二代祖北齊中書侍郎環俊以下，仕者相繼，而世牒具存焉。 子几。
In the chaos of the late Tang and Five Dynasties, many old gentry families left their home districts. Some had their lines of rank and office cut off, leaving their genealogies impossible to trace. Only the Liu clan, from their twelfth-generation ancestor Huanjun, Vice Director of the Secretariat under Northern Qi, onward, had officials succeeding one another across the generations, with their genealogical records fully preserved. His son Ji.
88
孫几
Grandson: Ji
89
几，字伯壽，以燁任為將作監主簿。 生而豪俊，長折節讀書，第進士。
Ji, whose style name was Boshou, entered office through Ye's yin privilege as Master Recorder of the Directorate of Imperial Works. Bold and spirited by nature, he later restrained himself and devoted himself to study, then passed the jinshi examination.
90
從范仲淹辟，通判邠州。 邠地鹵，民病遠汲，几浚渠引水注城中。 役興，客曰：“自郭汾陽城此州，苟外水可釃，何待今日？ 無為虛費勞人也！ ”几不答。 未幾，水果至，鑿五池於通逵，民大便利。
Recruited by Fan Zhongyan, he served as vice prefect of Bin Prefecture. Bin was a saline region, and the people suffered from having to draw water from far away. Ji dredged a canal to bring water into the city. When the project began, a visitor said, "Since Guo Ziyi fortified this prefecture, if water from outside could have been used, why wait until today? Do not waste labor in vain!" Ji did not reply. Before long the water did arrive. He excavated five ponds along the main thoroughfare, greatly benefiting the people.
91
孫沔薦其才堪將帥，換如京使、知寧州。 俗喜巫，軍校仗妖法結其徒，亂有日。 几使他兵伏壘門以伺，夜半盡禽之。 加本路兵馬鈐轄、知邠州。
Sun Mian recommended him as talented enough for command. He was transferred to Envoy of the Capital and appointed prefect of Ning Prefecture. The local people favored spirit-mediums. Military officers used occult arts to gather followers, and rebellion was imminent. Ji sent other troops to lie in wait at the camp gate and at midnight captured them all. He was additionally appointed Military Intendant of the circuit and prefect of Bin.
92
儂智高犯嶺南，几上書願自效，以為廣東、西捉殺。 道聞蔣偕、張忠戰沒，疾馳至長沙，見狄青曰：“賊若退守巢穴，瘴毒方興，當班師以俟再舉。 若恃勝求戰，此成擒耳。 ”賊果悉眾來，大戰於歸仁鋪。 前鋒孫節死，几以右軍搏鬥，自辰至巳，勝負未決。 几言於青，出勁騎五千，張左右翼搗其中堅，賊駭潰。
When Nong Zhigao invaded Lingnan, Ji submitted a memorial offering to serve and was made Pursuit-and-Suppression Commissioner of Guangdong and Guangxi. On the road he learned that Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had fallen in battle. He galloped to Changsha and told Di Qing, "If the rebels withdraw to their lair, miasma and pestilence will soon arise. The army should withdraw and wait for another campaign. If they grow overconfident and seek battle, they can be taken alive." The rebels indeed came with their entire force, and a great battle was fought at Guiren Station. The vanguard commander Sun Jie was killed. Ji fought with the right wing from mid-morning until late morning, and the outcome remained in doubt. Ji told Di Qing to deploy five thousand elite cavalry, spread left and right wings, and strike the enemy center. The rebels, terrified, broke and fled.
93
進皇城使、知涇州。 陛見，辭以母老，丐復文階歸養。 仁宗諭之曰：“涇，內地也，將母莫便焉。 ”命特賜冠帔。 領循州刺史，遷西上閣門使，再歸郎中班。 曾公亮薦之，復以嘉州團練使為太原、涇原路總管。
He was promoted to Commissioner of the Imperial City and appointed prefect of Jing Prefecture. At audience he declined the appointment on grounds of his aged mother and begged to return to civil rank so he could care for her. Emperor Renzong told him, "Jing is interior territory. Nowhere could be more convenient for bringing your mother." He ordered special gifts of cap and sash for Ji's mother. He concurrently served as prefect of Xunzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, and returned again to the Secretariat Gentleman roster. Zeng Gongliang recommended him, and he was again made Regimental Commissioner of Jia Prefecture and overall commander of the Taiyuan and Jingyuan circuits.

夏人寇周家堡，轉運使陳述古攝渭帥，几移文索援兵，不聽，率諸將偕請，又不聽，乃趣以手書。 述古怒，移几為鳳翔，且劾生事。 朝廷以總管非轉運使所得徙置，遣御史出按，述古黜，几亦改鄜州。 召判三班院。 邊吏告夏人趨大順，英宗問几。 几曰：“大順天險，非夏人可得近，正恐與趙明為仇爾。 ”帝曰：“明之子奔馬入城，幾為所掩，卿料敵一何神也。 ”以為秦鳳總管。
When the Tangut raided Zhoujiabao, Transport Commissioner Chen Shugu was acting as interim commander of Wei. Ji sent an official communication requesting reinforcements but was refused. He then led the generals in a joint request, again without success, and finally pressed the matter in a handwritten letter. Chen Shugu was furious. He transferred Ji to Fengxiang and also impeached him for stirring up trouble. The court ruled that an overall commander was not someone a transport commissioner could transfer at will. It dispatched an investigating censor, demoted Chen Shugu, and transferred Ji to Yan Prefecture. He was recalled to serve as chief judge of the Three Ranks Office. Border officials reported that the Tangut were advancing on Dashun. Emperor Yingzong asked Ji about it. Ji said, "Dashun is a natural stronghold that the Tangut cannot approach. I fear only that they mean to make an enemy of Zhao Ming." The emperor said, "Zhao Ming's son fled on horseback into the city and was nearly ambushed. How uncannily you read the enemy!" He was appointed overall commander of Qin and Feng.
95
神宗即位，轉四方館使、知保州，治狀為河北第一。 逾六年，即請老，還為秘書監致仕。 元豐三年，祀明堂，大臣言几知音，詔詣太常定雅樂。 几曰：“古樂備四清聲，沿五季亂離廢，請增之。 ”樂成，予一子官。
When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Ji was transferred to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and appointed prefect of Bao Prefecture. His record of governance ranked first in Hebei. After more than six years he immediately requested retirement and was granted the post of Retired Supervisor of the Secretariat. In the third year of Yuanfeng, during the Bright Hall sacrifice, ministers said Ji understood music, and an edict ordered him to the Court of Ceremonial to fix the court ritual music. Ji said, "Ancient music included all four clear tones, but they were abandoned in the chaos of the Five Dynasties. I request restoring them." When the music was completed, one of his sons was granted an official appointment.
96
几得謝二十年，放曠嵩、少間，遇唐末異人靖長宮者得養生訣，故益老不衰。 間與人語邊事，謂張耒曰：“比見詔書禁邊吏夜飲。 此曹一旦有急，將使輸其肝腦，此平日禁其為樂，為今役者不亦難乎？ 夫椎牛釃酒，豐犒而休養之，非欲以醉飽為德，所以增士氣也。 ”耒敬識其語。 再加通議大夫，卒，年八十一。
Ji enjoyed retirement for twenty years, living freely between Mount Song and Mount Shao. He met the Tang-dynasty recluse Jing Changgong and learned the secret of nourishing life, and so grew ever older without decline. From time to time, when discussing border affairs, he told Zhang Lei, "Recently I saw an edict forbidding border officials from drinking at night. When these men face sudden crisis, they will be asked to give their very lives. Yet in peacetime they are forbidden their pleasures. Under such circumstances, who will readily submit to today's orders?" Slaughtering cattle and libating wine, rewarding them generously and letting them rest—this is not meant to bestow the virtue of drunkenness and fullness. It is meant to raise morale. Zhang Lei respectfully noted his words. He was further promoted to Grand Master of Conferring Counsel and died at the age of eighty-one.
97
几篤於風義，推父遺恩官從兄，已得任子，必先兄弟子之孤者。 其議樂律最善，以為：“律主於人聲，不以尺度求合。 古今異時，聲亦隨變，猶以古冠服加於今人，安得而稱。 儒者泥古，致詳於形名度數間，而不知清濁輕重之用，故求於器雖合，而考於聲則不諧。 ”嘗遊佛寺，聞鍾聲，曰：“聲澌而悲，主者且不利。 ”是夕，主僧死。 在保州，聞角聲，曰：“宮微而商離，至秋，守臣憂之。 ”及期，几遇疾。 然所學頗雜鄭、衛云。
Ji was deeply devoted to the duties of friendship and honor. When extending his father's legacy of privilege appointments to a paternal cousin, he already had a yin appointment for his own son but always gave precedence to orphaned sons of his brothers. He was at his best when discussing musical pitch. He held that pitch pipes depend on the human voice and must not be forced into accord by measure and scale alone. Ancient times and the present differ, and sounds change with them. It is like putting ancient caps and robes on people today—how could they fit properly? Confucian scholars cling to antiquity, wrangling over nomenclature and measurement while ignoring the use of clear and murky, light and heavy tones. Thus though instruments may appear to accord, when tested by sound they prove disharmonious. Once while visiting a Buddhist temple he heard a bell and said, "The sound is breaking and mournful. The abbot will soon suffer misfortune." That evening the chief monk died. While at Bao Prefecture he heard horn signals and said, "The gong tone is faint and the shang tone is detached. By autumn the defending official will have cause for worry." When autumn came, Ji fell ill. Yet what he studied was somewhat mixed with the licentious music of Zheng and Wei.
98
劉濤，字德潤，徐州彭城人，後唐天成中，舉進士，釋褐為鳳翔掌書記，拜右拾遺，賜緋。 時太常丞史在德上章，詞理鄙俗，仍犯廟諱。 濤上言請正其罪，雖不允，時論是之。 出為山南東道節度判官，召為左補闕，遷起居舍人。
Liu Tao, whose style name was Derun, came from Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture. During the Tian Cheng era under Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination, took his first post as Recorder of Fengxiang, was appointed Right Remonstrating Censor, and was granted crimson robes. At the time Grand Master of Ceremonial Shi Zaide submitted a memorial whose language was coarse and who also violated the ancestral temple's taboo names. Tao submitted a memorial requesting that his offense be punished. Though the request was denied, contemporary opinion approved of Tao. He served as military adjutant of the Shannan East Circuit, was recalled as Left Supplementing Censor, and was promoted to Diarist.

晉天福初，改司勳員外郎、史館修撰，遷工部郎中，賜金紫。 歷度支、職方二郎中，掌左藏庫。 時少帝奢侈，常以銀易金，廣其器皿。 李崧判三司，令上庫金之數。 及崧以元簿較之，少數千鎰。 崧責曰：“帑庫通式，一日不受虛數，毫厘則有重典。 ”濤曰：“帑司常有報不盡數，以備宣索。 ”崧令有司劾濤，濤事迫，以情告樞密使桑維翰，乃止罰一月奉。 漢初，宰相蘇禹珪薦為中書舍人。
At the beginning of the Tian Fu era under Jin he was transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Merits and Compiler of the History Institute, promoted to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Works, and granted gold and purple robes. He served successively as Court Gentleman of the ministries of Revenue and of Military Appointments, and managed the Left Treasury. At the time the Young Emperor was extravagant and often exchanged silver for gold to enlarge his vessels. Li Song, as chief of the Three Departments, ordered an accounting of the gold in the upper treasury. When Li Song compared it with the original ledger, the count was short by several thousand yi. Li Song rebuked him, saying, "Treasury regulations do not tolerate false counts for even a single day. The slightest discrepancy brings severe punishment." Tao said, "Treasury officials often report incomplete counts to prepare for imperial requisitions." Li Song ordered the responsible office to impeach Tao. With the case pressing, Tao confided the facts to Military Affairs Commissioner Sang Weihan, and the punishment was limited to one month's salary. At the beginning of the Han dynasty, Chancellor Su Yudui recommended him for the post of Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
100
周廣順中，坐令子監察御史頊代草誥命，左遷少府少監，分司西京； 頊亦貶復州司戶。 顯德初，就改太常少卿，俄拜右諫議大夫。 四年，再知貢舉。 樞密使王樸嘗薦童子劉譜於濤，濤不納，樸銜之。 時世宗南征在迎鑾，濤引新及第人赴行在。 樸時留守上都，飛章言濤取士不精。 世宗命翰林學士李昉覆試，出者七人。 濤坐責授太子右讚善大夫。 恭帝即位，遷右詹事。 濤性剛毅不撓，素與宰相范質不協，常鬱鬱不得志，遂退居洛陽之清化里，杜門以書史自娛。
During the Guangshun era of Zhou, Tao was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshops and assigned to a subsidiary post at the Western Capital for having his son, Supervising Censor Xu, draft edicts on his behalf; Xu was also demoted to Registrar of Fu Prefecture. At the beginning of the Xiande era he was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and soon after was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master. In the fourth year he again supervised the civil service examinations. Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu once recommended the young candidate Liu Pu to Tao, but Tao did not accept him. Pu took offense. At the time Emperor Shizong was on his southern campaign at Yingluan, Tao led the newly passed candidates to the imperial camp. Pu, who was then left to guard the capital, sent an urgent memorial accusing Tao of selecting scholars without sufficient rigor. Emperor Shizong ordered Hanlin Academician Li Fang to conduct a re-examination, and seven candidates failed. Tao was punished and appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent. When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Tao was transferred to Right Household Mentor. Tao was firm and unyielding by nature. He had long been at odds with Chancellor Fan Zhi and often felt depressed and thwarted, so he retired to Qinghua Lane in Luoyang, shut his doors, and amused himself with books and history.
101
太祖素知濤履行，開寶二年召赴闕，以老病求退，授秘書監致仕。 年七十二卒。
Emperor Taizu had long known Tao's character. In the second year of Kaibao he was summoned to court, pleaded retirement on grounds of age and illness, and was granted the post of Director of the Secretariat with retirement honors. He died at the age of seventy-two.
102
清泰初，中書舍人盧導受詔主文，將鎖宿，濤力薦薛居正，以為文章器業必至臺輔，導取之，後果為相。 世稱其知人。
At the beginning of the Qingtai era, Drafting Secretary Lu Dao received an edict to preside over the examinations. As he was about to be sequestered, Tao strongly recommended Xue Juzheng, saying his literary talent and capacity would surely carry him to the highest offices. Dao selected him, and Xue later did indeed become chancellor. His contemporaries praised his discernment in judging men.
103
頊子晟，晟子訥、譚，並進士及第。 晟至屯田員外郎，訥為殿中侍御史。
Xu's son Sheng, and Sheng's sons Ne and Tan, all passed the jinshi examination. Sheng rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Agriculture, and Ne served as Palace Censor.
104
邊光範
Bian Guangfan
105
邊光範，字子儀，幷州陽曲人。 性謙退和雅，有吏材。 父仁嗣，忠武軍節度副使。 光範，後唐天成二年，起家榆次令，召為殿中丞，賜緋。 長興四年，改太常丞。 丁內艱。 晉天福初，服闋，授檢校戶部員外郎、北京留守判官兼侍御史。 二年，拜太府少卿。 上書曰：“臣聞唐太宗有言：‘朕居深宮之中，視聽不能及遠，所委者惟都督、刺史。 ’則知此官實係治亂，必須得人。 今則刺史或因緣世祿，或貢奉家財，或微立軍功，或但循官序。 實恐撫民無術，御吏無方，以此牧民，而民受其賜鮮矣。 望選能吏以蘇民瘼，用致升平。 ”奏入，留中不出。 俄為冊秦王李從嚴副使。 張從恩以外戚為河南尹，奏授判官。 遷秘書監兼御史中丞，入拜大理少卿。
Bian Guangfan, whose style name was Ziyi, came from Yangqu in Bing Prefecture. He was modest, retiring, and refined by nature, and possessed administrative talent. His father Rensi served as military vice commissioner of the Zhongwu Army. Guangfan began his career in the second year of Tiancheng under Later Tang as magistrate of Yuci. He was then summoned as Palace Aide and granted crimson robes. In the fourth year of Changxing he was transferred to Aide of the Ministry of Ceremonies. He entered mourning for his mother. At the beginning of the Tian Fu era under Jin, when his mourning ended, he was appointed Supernumerary Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, adjutant to the military governor of the Northern Capital, and concurrently Attending Censor. In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouses. He submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang said, 'I dwell deep within the palace. My sight and hearing cannot reach far, and those I entrust are only the regional commanders and prefectural governors. 'From this one knows that these offices truly bear on order and disorder, and the right men must be found. Today prefectural governors may obtain office through hereditary privilege, by presenting family wealth as tribute, through slight military merit, or merely by advancing in the official sequence. I truly fear they have no method for comforting the people and no way to control officials. Governing the people in this manner, the people receive little benefit. I hope that able administrators may be selected to relieve the people's distress and thereby bring about peace and order. "The memorial was submitted but kept within the palace without response. Soon after he served as deputy envoy in the investiture of Prince Qin Li Congyan. Zhang Cong'en, as a maternal relative of the emperor, served as Intendant of Henan and memorialized to appoint Guangfan as his adjutant. He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, then entered court and was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
106
漢初，改檢校刑部尚書、衛尉卿。 上言：“伏見朝廷除刺史，不限年月，或未及期年，又聞除代。 往來跋涉，豈暇撫懷。 望慎選良牧，立定年限，以責輯綏之效。 ”疏入，不報。 乾祐二年，連使宋州虞城、汝州襄城，按視民田之傷稼者。 是冬，為吳越加恩使。
At the beginning of the Han dynasty he was transferred to Supernumerary Minister of Punishments and Commandant of the Guard. He submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject observes that when the court appoints prefectural governors, no fixed term is set. Sometimes before a full year has passed, word comes of a replacement. Traveling back and forth on long journeys, how can they find leisure to comfort and care for the people? I hope that good governors may be carefully selected and fixed terms established, so that they may be held accountable for pacifying and governing their districts. "The memorial was submitted but received no response. In the second year of Qianyou he was sent in succession to Yucheng in Song Prefecture and Xiangcheng in Ru Prefecture to inspect civilian fields where crops had been damaged. That winter he served as envoy to confer additional honors on Wuyue.
107
周廣順初，出知陳州，遷秘書監，俄召拜御史中丞，賜襲衣、銀器、繒彩、鞍勒馬，復為禮部侍郎。 時禮部侍郎於貢部或掌或否，光範拜官，將及秋試，乃言於執政曰：“單門偶進，何言名第。 若他曹公事，光範不敢辭； 若處文衡，校閱名賢，品藻優劣，非下走所能。 ”執政曰：“公晉末為翰林、樞密直學士，勿避事也。 ”及期，光節辭疾不出，乃以翰林學士承旨徐台符掌之，時論多其自知。
At the beginning of the Guangshun era under Zhou he went out as prefect of Chen Prefecture and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat. Soon after he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief, granted ceremonial robes, silver vessels, silk brocade, and a saddled horse, and again served as Vice Minister of Rites. At the time the Vice Minister of Rites sometimes did and sometimes did not oversee the examination bureau. Guangfan received his appointment as the autumn examinations drew near and said to the chief ministers, "From a humble household I happened to advance—what claim have I to rank and degree? If it is ordinary business of another office, I would not dare refuse; but if I am to sit at the literary scales, examine eminent scholars, and judge their excellence and inferiority, that is beyond what one of my station can do. "The chief ministers said, "Sir, at the end of Jin you served as Hanlin academician and direct academician of the Military Affairs Bureau. Do not shirk your duty. "When the time came, Guangfan pleaded illness and did not appear. Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Xu Taifu was then put in charge, and contemporary opinion largely approved Guangfan's self-knowledge.
108
宋初，征澤、潞，命光範為前軍轉運，計度鄭、洛、汝、孟、懷芻糧。 秋，拜太常卿。 時張昭為吏部尚書，朝議以其耆老，令光範簽判選事。
At the beginning of the Song dynasty, when Ze and Lu were being attacked, Guangfan was ordered to serve as transport commissioner for the vanguard army, calculating and provisioning fodder and grain for Zheng, Luo, Ru, Meng, and Huai. In autumn he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies. At the time Zhang Zhao was Minister of Personnel. Considering his advanced age, the court had Guangfan countersign and decide selection matters.
109
建隆四年，襄州節度慕容延釗征湖南，以光範權知州事，路當衝會，餉饋無闕。 是冬郊祀，召還。 會延釗卒，復知襄州。 大軍數萬由陝路討蜀，出漢上，光範復當供億，人不知勞。 嘗舉本鎮判官李楫為殿中侍御史，楫後坐事除籍，光範左遷太子賓客，仍知襄州。
In the fourth year of Jianlong, when Military Commissioner Murong Yanzhao of Xiang Prefecture campaigned in Hunan, Guangfan was appointed acting prefect. The route lay at a strategic junction, and supplies were never lacking. That winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he was recalled. When Yanzhao died, he again served as prefect of Xiang Prefecture. An army of tens of thousands marched by the Shaan route to attack Shu, emerging onto the Han River. Guangfan again took charge of provisioning, and the people felt no hardship. He once recommended his circuit's adjutant Li Ji as Palace Censor. Ji was later implicated in an offense and struck from the rolls, and Guangfan was demoted to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent while still serving as prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
110
五年，兼橋道使，朝廷遣使督治道，常六七輩，一使所調發民皆數百人，吏緣為奸，多私取民課，所發不充數，而道益不修。 光範計其工，以州卒代民，官給器用，役不淹久，人以無擾。 詔書褒美。 開寶四年，復判吏部銓曹。 御史中丞劉溫叟卒，以光範判御史臺事，數月，真拜中丞。 六年，以疾解銓曹任。 卒，年七十三。
In the fifth year he concurrently served as Commissioner for Bridge Roads. The court sent envoys to supervise road repair, often six or seven at a time. Each envoy's requisition mobilized several hundred civilians. Officials used this as a pretext for corruption and often privately seized civilian labor dues. What was mobilized fell short of the quota, and the roads grew ever more unrepaired. Guangfan calculated the labor required, used prefectural soldiers in place of civilians, and had the government supply tools. The service did not drag on, and the people were undisturbed. An edict praised him. In the fourth year of Kaibao he again served as acting chief of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau. When Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou died, Guangfan was appointed acting chief of the Censorate. After several months he was formally appointed Censor-in-Chief. In the sixth year he relinquished his post in the selection bureau on grounds of illness. He died at the age of seventy-three.
111
光範性至孝，謙退和易，雅有吏幹。 母病疽，光範嘗吮之。 景德中，錄其孫易從同學究出身。
Guangfan was profoundly filial by nature. He was modest, retiring, and easy in manner, and possessed refined administrative ability. When his mother suffered from a carbuncle, Guangfan once sucked the wound. During the Jingde era his grandson Yicong was granted entry through the same xuejiu qualification.
112
劉載，字德輿，涿州范陽人。 唐盧龍節度濟之六世孫。 父昭，下蔡令。 載，後唐清泰中舉進士。 晉初，解褐校書郎，遷著作佐郎，賜緋，拜左拾遺、集賢殿直學士。 漢初，為殿中侍卿御史，丁內艱，服闋，復拜舊官。 判西京留臺，改倉部員外郎。 嘗著五論，曰《為君》、《為相》、《為將》、《去讒》、《納諫》，頗為文士所稱。
Liu Zai, whose style name was Deyu, came from Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture. He was the sixth-generation descendant of Ji, military commissioner of Lulong under Tang. His father Zhao served as magistrate of Xia Cai. Zai passed the jinshi examination during the Qingtai era under Later Tang. At the beginning of the Jin dynasty he entered service as Collator, was promoted to Assistant Compiler, granted crimson robes, and appointed Left Remonstrance Censor and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. At the beginning of the Han dynasty he served as Palace Attending Censor. After entering mourning for his mother, when mourning ended he was again appointed to his former office. He served as administrative aide to the Western Capital's Retired Emperor's Pavilion and was transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Granaries. He once composed five treatises titled "On Being a Ruler," "On Being a Chancellor," "On Being a General," "On Removing Slander," and "On Accepting Remonstrance," and they were much praised by literary men.
113
周世宗初，擢知制誥。 顯德三年，拜右諫議大夫，與右拾遺鄭起、尚書博士李寧同校道書。 遷給事中，使許州定田租。 俄賜金紫，為魏王符彥卿加恩國信使。
At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was promoted to Drafting Edicts. In the third year of Xiande he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master and, together with Right Remonstrance Censor Zheng Qi and Erudite of the Masters of Documents Li Ning, collated Daoist texts. He was promoted to Supervising Censor and sent to Xu Prefecture to fix land tax assessments. Soon after he was granted gold and purple robes and served as credentialed envoy to confer additional honors on Prince Wei Fu Yanqing.
114
宋初，浚五丈河，自陳橋達曹州之西境，命護其役。 建隆四年，貝州節度使張光翰來朝，遣載權知州事。 光翰歸鎮，載還，知貢舉。 乾德初，掌建安榷貨務。 六年，就為江南國主生辰使，召還，令知鎮州。
At the beginning of the Song dynasty the Wuzhang River was dredged from Chenqiao to the western border of Cao Prefecture, and he was ordered to oversee the work. In the fourth year of Jianlong, Military Commissioner Zhang Guanghan of Bei Prefecture came to court, and Zai was dispatched to serve as acting prefect. When Guanghan returned to his command, Zai came back and supervised the civil service examinations. At the beginning of the Qiande era he managed the Jian'an Commodity Monopoly Office. In the sixth year he served as birthday envoy to the lord of Jiangnan, was recalled, and was ordered to serve as prefect of Zhen Prefecture.
115
開寶四年，坐與何繼筠不協，改山南東道行軍司馬。 十年不召，嘗受詔權點檢州事。 太平興國初，復入為給事中。 三年，出知襄州，六年，代還。 告老，改工部侍郎致仕，乃賜一子出身。 八年，卒，年七十一。
In the fourth year of Kaibao, for being at odds with He Jiyun, he was transferred to Military Administrator of the Shannan East Circuit. For ten years he was not summoned to court. He once received an edict to act as inspector of prefectural affairs. At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he again entered court as Supervising Censor. In the third year he went out as prefect of Xiang Prefecture. In the sixth year he was replaced and returned. He requested retirement on grounds of age, was transferred to Vice Minister of Works with retirement honors, and one son was granted entry qualification. In the eighth year he died at the age of seventy-one.
116
載尤好學，博通史傳，善屬文。 嘗受詔撰明憲皇后諡冊文，又作《吊戰國賦》萬餘言行於世。 雅信釋典，敦尚名節。
Zai was especially fond of learning, thoroughly versed in historical records and biographies, and skilled at literary composition. He once received an edict to compose the posthumous-title document for Empress Mingxian, and also wrote "Lament for the Warring States," more than ten thousand characters in length, which circulated widely. He deeply believed in Buddhist scriptures and earnestly upheld reputation and integrity.
117
子宗言，至比部郎中。 宗望，景德二年進士及第。 大中祥符四年，其孫介以載文集來獻，以為試將作主簿。
His son Zongyan rose to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue. Zongwang passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingde. In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his grandson Jie presented Zai's collected writings and was made Trial Assistant Magistrate of the General's Office.
118
程羽，字冲遠，深州陸澤人。 少好學，能屬文。 晉天福中，擢進士第，授陽穀主簿。 歷虞鄉、醴泉、新都令，皆有政績。 開寶中，選為兩使判官，入對，太祖詢以時事，敷奏稱旨，擢著作郎，出知興州。 逾年，改知興元府。 八年，詔歸闕，以本官領開封府判官。
Cheng Yu, whose style name was Chongyuan, came from Luze in Shen Prefecture. From youth he loved learning and could compose literary works. During the Tian Fu era under Jin he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yanggu. He served successively as magistrate of Yuxiang, Liquan, and Xindu, and achieved notable results in each post. During the Kaibao era he was selected as adjutant to a diplomatic envoy. At audience Emperor Taizu questioned him on current affairs, and his full presentation accorded with the emperor's intent. He was promoted to Compiler and sent out as prefect of Xing Prefecture. After more than a year he was made administrator of Xingyuan Prefecture. In the eighth year an edict recalled him to court, and he served as chief judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture while retaining his original rank.
119
羽性淳厚，蒞事恪謹。 時太宗尹京，頗以長者待之。 及即位，拜給事中，知開封府。 未幾，出知成都府，為政寬簡，蜀人便之。 入朝，拜禮部侍郎。 上欲優以清職。 故事，端明殿設學士二員，居翰林學士上，專備顧問，馮道、趙鳳始居是職，累朝因之。 及是，即殿名以羽為文明殿學士，位在樞密副使下，且即泰寧坊營第以賜之。
Yu was sincere and generous by nature and handled affairs with scrupulous care. At that time the future Taizong governed the capital and treated him with the respect due an elder. When he took the throne, Yu was appointed Supervising Censor and put in charge of Kaifeng Prefecture. Before long he was sent out as administrator of Chengdu Prefecture. His government was lenient and simple, and the people of Shu found it agreeable. He returned to court and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites. The emperor wished to honor him with a prestigious, purely advisory post. By precedent the Hall of Illuminated Clarity had two academicians who ranked above Hanlin academicians and served solely as imperial advisers. Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were the first to hold these posts, and successive dynasties followed the practice. On this occasion, taking the hall's name, Yu was made Academician of the Hall of Civilization, ranking below the vice commissioner of Military Affairs, and a residence was built for him in Taining Ward and granted to him.
120
太平興國五年，典試貢士，御試得人居多。 六年，以老疾求解職，拜兵部侍郎，未幾致仕，仍給全奉。 雍熙元年，卒，年七十二。 贈禮部尚書。
In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he presided over the civil service examinations, and many of those chosen in the imperial examination were men he had recommended. In the sixth year, citing old age and illness, he asked to leave office, was appointed Vice Minister of War, and soon retired while continuing to receive his full salary. In the first year of Yongxi he died at the age of seventy-two. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
121
子希振，以蔭至尚書虞部員外郎。 大中祥符元年卒。 其子適，賜同學究出身。 從孫琳，別傳。
His son Xizhen, through hereditary privilege, rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Parks Office. He died in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu. His son Shi was granted the qualification of a fellow licentiate. His collateral descendant Lin is treated in a separate biography.
122
論曰：五季為國，不四、三傳輒易姓，其臣子視事君猶傭者焉，主易則他役，習以為常。 故唐方滅即北面於晉，漢甫稱禪已相率下拜於周矣。 君子傷之，此《雜臣傳》所繇立也。 李穀、邊歸讜、竇貞固、李濤輩，或在廟堂，或侍帷幄，世主之所寵任，社稷之所倚賴，而更事異姓，不能以名節生死，倫義廢矣。 且穀以籌策自名，乃不能料藝祖有容人之量，及受李筠饋遺，懼其見殺，遂以憂死，又何繆耶？ 嗚呼，魏范粲、齊顏見遠，宜見褒於前史也。
The commentary says: During the Five Dynasties, within three or four generations a ruling house would change surname. Ministers treated service to a ruler like hired labor: when the master changed they took another post, and this became habitual. Thus when Tang had just fallen they at once submitted to Jin, and when Han had barely claimed the throne they were already bowing in succession to Zhou. Men of principle grieved at this, which is why the "Biographies of Miscellaneous Ministers" was established. Li Gu, Bian Guidang, Dou Zhengu, Li Tao, and men like them—some in the halls of government, some attending within the imperial curtain—were favorites of their rulers and pillars on whom the state relied. Yet they served houses of different surnames and could not live or die for reputation and integrity; moral duty was cast aside. Moreover, Gu had made his name by strategy, yet failed to foresee that Taizu had the magnanimity to tolerate others. When he accepted Li Yun's gifts and feared execution, he died of grief—how mistaken was that? Alas, Fan Can of Wei and Yan Jianyuan of Qi deserved praise in the earlier histories.
